21:1: God the Almighty says: The reckoning of people has drawn near regarding the deeds they did in their worldly life and the blessings He bestowed upon them in it in their bodies, their bodies, their food, their drink, their clothing and other blessings He bestowed upon them. His question to them is: What did they do in it? Did they obey Him in it and abide by His commands and prohibitions in all of it, or did they disobey Him and go against His commands in it? And they are in heedlessness, turning away. He says: And they are in this world from what God will do to them on the Day of Resurrection, and from the approach of His reckoning of them and His drawing near to them in heedlessness and negligence. They have turned away from that, so they have abandoned thinking about it, preparing for it, and getting ready out of ignorance of what they will encounter at that time of great affliction and severe terrors. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, And they are in heedlessness turning away, the people of interpretation said, and the trace came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Walid told us: Abu Muawiyah told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And they are in heedlessness, turning away. He said: In this world.
21:2: God Almighty says: God does not send down anything of this Qur’an to the people, nor does He remind them of it and admonish them, except that they listen to it while they are playing, their hearts distracted. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, There comes not to them a reminder from their Lord renewed, the verse, he says: Nothing of the Qur’an is sent down to them except that they listen to it while they are playing.
21:3: God Almighty says, Their hearts are heedless, heedless. He says: These people, whose description is described in this Qur’an, do not listen except while they are playing, their hearts heedless of it, they do not ponder its ruling, nor do they reflect on the arguments that God has deposited against them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Their hearts are heedless, he said: Their hearts are neglectful. And His statement, And those who did wrong whispered secretly, meaning, these people, for whom the Hour is approaching, while they are heedless and turning away, their hearts distracted, whispered secretly among themselves. He says, “And they revealed their secret conversation among themselves, saying: Is this he who claims that he is a messenger from God sent to you, anything but a human being like you? They say: Is he anything but a human being like you in your appearance and creation?” They mean by that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And those who did wrong said, so He described them as wrongdoing, and what He informed about them in these verses is that they do and say what they say, turning away from the remembrance of God and denying His Messenger. As for those who in his saying And those who did wrong whispered secretly in the parsing there are two aspects: the accusative because it is a follower of the people in his saying Their reckoning has drawn near for the people and the nominative because of the response from the names who in his saying And those who did wrong whispered secretly from the mention of the people as it was said: Then many of them became blind and deaf (al-Ma’idah 5:71). It may be possible that it is nominative as the beginning, and its meaning is and they whispered secretly, then he said: They are those who did wrong. And His statement, Do you then practice magic while you are seeing? means: And they revealed this statement among themselves, which is the secret conversation that they kept secret among themselves, so some of them said to others: Do you accept magic and believe in it while you know that it is magic? They meant by that the Qur’an. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Do you then practice magic while you see? He said: The people of disbelief said this to their prophet when he brought it from God. They claimed that he was a magician, and that what he brought was magic. They said: Do you practice magic while you see?
21:4: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, Say, my Lord. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, recited, Say, my Lord, as a command. Some of the reciters of Mecca, and the majority of the Kufians, recited, My Lord said, as a statement. It is as if those who read it as a command meant by its interpretation: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say, Do you then practice magic while you are seeing? My Lord knows the saying of every speaker in the heaven and the earth. Nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the Hearer of all of that, and of what they say of lies. He is the Knower of my truthfulness and the reality of what I call you to, and the falsehood of what you say, and other than that of all things. It is as if those who read it as a statement meant, Muhammad said: My Lord knows the saying, as report from God about the answer of His Prophet to them. The statement about that is that they are two well-known readings in the reading of the regions, and each one of them was read by scholars of the readers, and the Muslims’ Qur’ans came with them agreeing in meaning, and that is because if God wanted Muhammad to say that, He said it, and if He said it, then He said it by the command of God, so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct in his recitation.
21:5: God the Most High says: They did not believe in the wisdom of this Qur’an, nor that it is from God, nor did they acknowledge that it is a revelation that God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, some of them said: It is a vision that he saw in his sleep. Some of them said: It is a lie and fabrication that he invented and fabricated on his own. Some of them said: Rather, Muhammad is a poet, and what he brought to you is poetry. So let him come to us means: They said: So let Muhammad come to us if he is truthful in what he says, that God sent him as a messenger to us, and that what he recites to us is a revelation from God that He revealed to us. With a sign means: With an argument and proof of the truth of what he says and claims. As the former messengers were sent means: As the former messengers before him brought it, such as reviving the dead, healing the blind and the leper, and the she-camel of Salih, and other similar miracles that only God is capable of, and that only the prophets and messengers can bring. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, confused dreams, meaning the action of a dreamer, it is only a vision he saw. Rather, he invented it, rather, he is a poet. All of this was from them. And his statement, Then let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent, he says: as Jesus came with clear proofs and Moses came with clear proofs, and the messengers. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, confused dreams, he said: ambiguous. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, and he said: Confused dreams, he said: Its horrors. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And God Almighty said: Rather, they said: And there is no apparent denial in the speech, so it is confirmed by rather, because the report is about people of denial and lying, so it is sufficient to know the listeners with what is indicated by His statement: Rather, from the mention of the report about them, as we have explained.
21:6: God Almighty says: None of those who denied Muhammad before, from the polytheists of his people, believed in him. They said: Let Muhammad bring us a sign like the messengers before him from the people of a town whom We punished with destruction in this world, when Our Messenger came to them with a miraculous sign. Do they believe? He says: Will these who denied Muhammad, who asked him for a sign, believe in him if a sign came to them, while their ancestors before them from the past nations whom We destroyed with their messengers did not believe with their coming. In a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, “We destroyed it. Will they believe?” They will believe in that. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “No town which We destroyed believed before them. Will they believe?” That is, the messengers, when they came to their people with clear proofs and they did not believe, were not given respite.
21:7: God the Almighty says to His Prophet: We did not send, O Muhammad, a messenger to any nation that passed before your nation except men like them, to whom We revealed what We wanted to reveal to them of Our commands and prohibitions, not angels. So why did they deny that We sent you to them, while you are a man like all the messengers who came before you to their nations? And His statement: So ask the people of the message if you do not know means to those who said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their private conversations among themselves: Is this not a human being like you? If you deny and are ignorant of the matter of the messengers who came before Muhammad, and you do not know, O people, whether they were human or angels, then ask the people of the Books from the Torah and the Gospel what they used to tell you about them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: So ask the people of the message if you do not know means: So ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel - Abu Ja`far said: I think he said: - They will tell you that the messengers were men who ate food and walked in the markets. It was said: The people of remembrance are the people of the Qur’an. Who said that? Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me: Abd al-Rahman bin Salih told me: Musa bin Uthman told me, on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi, who said: When the verse So ask the people of the message if you do not know was revealed, Ali said: We are the people of the message. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: So ask the people of the message if you do not know, he said: The people of the Qur’an, and the message is the Qur’an, and he recited: Indeed, it is We who sent down the message and indeed, We will be its guardian.
21:8: God Almighty says: And We did not make the messengers whom We sent before you, O Muhammad, to the past nations before your nation bodies that do not eat food. He says: We did not make them angels that do not eat food, but We made them bodies like you that eat food. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, meaning: I did not make them bodies that did not have souls in them that did not eat food, but rather We made them bodies that had souls in them that ate food. Abu Ja`far said: He said: And We did not make them a body, so he made the body unified and made it unified, and it is from the description of the group, and this is permissible because the body means the source, as is said in speech: And We did not make them a creation that does not eat. And His statement: And they were not immortal means: Nor were they lords who do not die or perish, but they were human bodies and then died. This is because they said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God informed us about them: We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth... until His statement: Or you bring God and the angels as a face. God Almighty said to them: We did not do that to anyone before you so that we would do it to you. Rather, We sent to them men to whom We revealed just as We sent to you a Messenger to whom We revealed Our commands and prohibitions. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they will not be immortal: meaning, they will inevitably die.
21:9: God the Most High says: Then We confirmed Our messengers whom their nations denied, and asked them for signs, so We gave them what they asked for, then they persisted in their denial of her, and insisted on their denial of her prophethood after what she brought them of the signs of her Lord, and We promised them what We promised them of destruction for their persistence in disbelieving in their Lord after the coming of the sign that they asked of Him, and that is like His saying, the Most High: So whoever disbelieves among you, then I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone in the worlds (al-Ma’idah 5:115) and His saying: And do not touch her with harm, lest a near punishment seize you and similar to that of the promises that He promised the nations with the coming of the signs. And His saying: So We saved them means, the Most High: So We saved the messengers when their nations persisted in denying her after the signs, and whomever We willed and they are her followers who believed in her and had faith in her. And His statement, And We destroyed the transgressors, God Almighty says: And We destroyed those who transgressed against themselves by disbelieving in their Lord. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We destroyed the transgressors. The transgressors are the polytheists.
21:10: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: Its meaning is, We have sent down to you a book in which is your remembrance, in which is your speech. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, In it is your mention, he said: your hadith. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. He said: Your speech. Do you not then reason? He said in: He has succeeded. Rather, We have brought them their remembrance, but they are turning away from their remembrance. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Sufyan told us, the Qur’an was revealed with noble morals. Did you not hear Him say, “Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. Will you not then reason?” Others said: Rather, what is meant by the mention in this place is: honor. They said: The meaning of the statement is: We have sent down to you a book about your honor. Abu Jaafar said: This second statement is more similar to the meaning of the word, and it is similar to what Sufyan said, whom we have narrated from, and that is that it is an honor for whoever follows it and acts according to what is in it.
21:11: God Almighty says: And many a town have We destroyed. The root of the word qasm is breaking. It is said: I broke the back of so-and-so if you break it. And anqasamat sanah if it is broken. Here it means We destroyed. And the people of interpretation interpreted it in this way. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And how many have We destroyed, he said: We have destroyed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And how many a town have We destroyed, he said: We have annihilated it. Ibn Jurayj said: We have destroyed a town, he said: In Yemen we destroyed, they were destroyed by the sword. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding God’s statement, We destroyed a city, he said: He destroyed it, he destroyed it. And His statement, From a town that was unjust, He made the speech apply to the town, and what is meant by it is its people, so that the listeners would know its meaning. And its injustice was its disbelief in God and its denial of His messengers. And His statement, And We brought forth after it another people, God Almighty says: And after We destroyed these unjust people from the people of this town, which We destroyed with its injustice, We brought forth another people besides them. His saying, When they sensed Our punishment, means: When they witnessed Our punishment descending upon them, and saw it, they felt its touch. It is said from it: I sensed weakness from so-and-so, and I sensed it from him. When they were about to run from it, means: When they sensed Our punishment descending upon them, they fled quickly and hastily, running in defeat. It is said from it: So-and-so ran his horse, meaning he pushed it with his driving.
21:12: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So when they perceived Our might, at once they were running from it.
21:13: God Almighty says: Do not flee, but return to the luxury in which you lived: He says: to the luxury in which you lived and your dwellings. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Do not run, but return to what you enjoyed and your dwellings, that you may be questioned. He means those upon whom punishment descended in this world from among the nations who disobeyed God. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Do not run means do not flee. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And return to what you enjoyed in luxury. He said: Return to your worldly life in which you enjoyed luxury. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And return to what you enjoyed of luxury. He said: To what you enjoyed of your worldly life. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying, Perhaps you will ask. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Perhaps you will understand and comprehend through the question. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Perhaps you will ask, he said: You will understand. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Perhaps you will ask, he said, you will understand. Others said: Rather, its meaning is that you may ask for something from your worldly life in a mocking and derisive manner. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps you will ask is mocking them. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me: Muhammad bin Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps you will ask for something from your world, mocking them.
21:14: God the Most High says: When God's punishment descended upon them, those upon whom God's punishment descended due to their injustice said: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers, because we disbelieved in our Lord. And that was their cry, meaning their cry did not cease, when God's punishment came upon them due to their injustice to themselves: Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers until God killed them, harvesting them with the sword as a crop is harvested and uprooted with sickles. And His statement: quiet means: perishing, their spark was extinguished and their movement ceased, so they became inert as a fire is extinguished and then put out. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And that was their call... the verse, so when they saw the punishment and witnessed it, they had no recourse except their saying, Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers, until God destroyed them and their families. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ And that was their cry until We made them like a harvest, extinguished. He said: until they perished. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abbas said: Harvested is the harvest, quiet is the extinguishing of the fire when it is extinguished. Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They were people of fortresses, and God sent Nebuchadnezzar against them, so he sent an army to them and killed them with the sword, and they killed a prophet of theirs and harvested with the sword, and that is what He said: And that was their cry until We made them a harvest, extinguished with the sword.
21:15: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And that was their call until We made them a harvest, extinguished.
21:16: God Almighty says: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them except as an argument against you, O people, and so that you may consider all of this, and learn that the One Who planned and created it is not like anything, and that divinity is only for Him, and worship is not appropriate for anything other than Him, and He did not create this in vain and play. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play, meaning: We did not create them in vain or in vain.
21:17: God Almighty says: If we wanted to take a wife and a child, we would have taken that from ourselves, but we do not do that, and it is not appropriate for us to do it, and it is not appropriate, because it is not appropriate for God to have a child or a companion. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Sulayman bin Ubayd God al-Ghaidani told me: Abu Qutaybah told us: Salam bin Maskeen told us: Uqbah bin Abi Hamza told us: I witnessed al-Hasan in Mecca. Tawus, Ata’ and Mujahid came to him and asked him about the statement of God Almighty: If We had intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it. Al-Hasan said: Diversion means women. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me: Baqiyah bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Harun, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: If We had wanted to take a diversion, he said: A wife. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: If we were to do it, meaning: We were not to do it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: They said: Mary was his companion, and Jesus was his son, so the Blessed and Exalted said: If We had wanted to take a diversion women and children We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were to do so. He said: From Our presence, and We did not create Paradise or Hell, nor death, nor resurrection, nor reckoning. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: We would have taken him from Our presence from Our presence, and We did not create Paradise or Hell, nor death nor resurrection.
21:18: God Almighty says: But We send down the truth from Us, and it is the Book of God, and its revelation is upon the disbelievers in it and their people, and it destroys him: He says: It destroys him as a man destroys another man by striking him on the head with a wound that reaches the brain, and if the wound reaches that of the wounded person, he will have no life after that. And his saying: Then it will perish, means: Then it will perish and disappear. As Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then he is doomed. He said: He is lost. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and at once it departs. The truth is the Book of God, the Qur’an, and falsehood is Satan, so He destroys it, and at once it departs: that is, it goes away. And His statement: And woe to you for what you describe. He says: And woe to you for your describing your Lord with a description other than His, and your saying that He took a wife and a son, and your slander against Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, except that some of them said: The meaning of you describe is you lie. Others said: The meaning of this is: you associate, and even if the words differ, their meanings are the same, because whoever describes God as having a companion has lied in describing Him with that, and has associated with Him, and described Him with something other than His attribute. However, the most appropriate expressions to express the meanings of the Qur’an are those closest to the understanding of its listeners. Mention of those who said what we said about that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And for you is woe for what you describe means that you lie. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And for you is woe for what you describe. He said: You associate others with God. And His statement: For what they describe. He said: They associate others with God. He said: And Mujahid said: He will recompense them for their description. Al-An`am: 139. He said: Their statement is a lie in that.
21:19: God Almighty says: How can it be permissible for God to be taken as a pastime, while He owns all those in the heavens and the earth, and those of His creation who are with Him do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they refrain from worshipping Him because of their long service to Him, and you know that He does not enslave a father or a wife to his son, and all those in the heavens and the earth are His slaves, so how can He have a wife and a child? He says: Or do you not reflect on what you invent of lies against your Lord? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And they do not regret means they do not regret. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And they do not become weary, he said: They do not become exhausted. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And they do not become weary, he said: they do not become exhausted. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: They are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they grow weary, he said: They do not grow weary, they do not tire of that wearying, he said: And they do not slacken, nor do they become tired, all of this has the same meaning, but the speech is different, and it is from their saying: a weary camel: if it becomes exhausted and stands up, and from it is the saying of Alqamah to Abda: It has corpses of sorrow, but its bones are white, and its skin is black.
21:20: God Almighty says: These angels who are with Him glorify their Lord night and day, never slackening in their glorification of Him. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka`b about his statement: They glorify God night and day, never slackening, and they glorify God night and day, never tiring. He said: Does your glance tire you, does your soul tire you? He said: No. He said: Then they were inspired to glorify God just as they were inspired to glance and to breathe. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated: Abu Ishaq Al-Shaibani narrated: Hassan bin Mukhariq narrated: Abdullah bin Al-Harith said: I said to Ka’b Al-Ahbar: They glorify God night and day, never slackening. Doesn’t a message or work occupy them? He said: O son of my brother, glorification has been made for them, just as speech has been made for the soul. Do you not eat and drink, stand and sit, come and go, and you breathe? I said: Yes. He said: So glorification has been made for them. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman and Abu Dawud told us: Imran al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Amr al-Bakali, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: God created ten parts. He made nine parts glorify Him day and night without slackening, and one part for His message, and the creation part is ten parts, and He made nine parts the jinn, and one part the rest of the children of Adam, and the children of Adam are ten parts, and He made Gog and Magog nine parts, and one part the rest of the children of Adam. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: They glorify Him night and day, never slackening, meaning: The angels who are with the Most Merciful do not disdain His worship, nor do they become weary of it. He told us that while the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with his companions, he said, Do you hear what I hear? They said, We do not hear anything, O Prophet of God. He said, I hear the creaking of the sky, and it is not to be blamed for creaking, and there is no place of rest in it except that there is an angel prostrating or standing in it. And His statement: Or have they taken gods from the earth who resurrect? God Almighty says: Have these polytheists taken gods from the earth who resurrect? He means by His statement: they: the gods. He says: These gods that they have taken resurrect the dead. He says: They bring the dead to life and resurrect creation. For God is the One who gives life and causes death. As Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us (H), and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: they will spread out means: they will love. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement: Or have they taken gods from the earth who resurrect? He said: Is there among their gods anyone who gives life to that which they resurrect? And he recited the statement of God: “Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?” Yunus 10:31 until His statement: What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Yunus 10:35.
21:21: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Or have they taken gods from the earth who are resurrecting?
21:22: God Almighty says: If there were in the heavens and the earth gods who were worthy of worship other than God, who is the Creator of all things, and to Him belongs worship and divinity that is only fitting for Him, they would have been ruined. He says: The people of the heavens and the earth would have been ruined. So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. God Almighty says: So He is glorified and exonerated from what these polytheists fabricate against Him of lies. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “If there had been within them gods besides God, they both would have been ruined. So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.” He glorifies Himself when slander was said about Him.
21:23: God Almighty says: No questioner asks the Lord of the Throne about what He does with His creation, in terms of disposing of them as He wills of life and death, honor and humiliation, and other than that of His judgment over them, because they are His creation and His servants, and all of them are under His dominion and authority, and the judgment is His judgment, and the decree is His decree, and nothing is above Him to ask Him about what He does, and He says to Him: Why did you do it? And why did you not do it? And they will be questioned. God Almighty says: And all of His servants in the heavens and the earth are responsible for their actions, and are held accountable for their deeds, and He is the One who asks them about that, and holds them accountable for it, because He is above them and their Owner, and they are under His authority. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned, meaning: He is not questioned about what He does with His servants, but they will be questioned about their deeds. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: His statement: He will not be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned, he said: The Creator will not be questioned about His judgment on His creation, but He will question the creation about their actions. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned, he said: The Creator is not questioned about what He decrees for His creation, and the creation is responsible for their actions.
21:24: God Almighty says: These polytheists have taken gods besides God who benefit and harm, create and give life and cause death. Say, O Muhammad, to them: Bring your proof, meaning your argument. He says: Bring, if you claim that you are right in what you say, an argument and proof of your truthfulness. As Bishr narrated, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “Say: Bring your proof,” meaning: Bring your evidence for what you say. And His statement: This is a reminder of those with me, meaning: This is what I have brought to you from God of the Qur’an and revelation. A reminder of those with me, meaning: report of those with me of what they will have of God’s reward for their belief in Him and their obedience to Him, and what they will be subject to of God’s punishment for their disobedience to Him and their disbelief in Him. And a reminder of those before me, meaning: report of those before me of the nations that came before me, and what God did to them in this world and what He will do to them in the Hereafter. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: This is a reminder of those with me, this Qur’an says in mentioning what is lawful and what is unlawful. And a reminder of those before me, he says: a reminder of the deeds of previous nations and what God did to them and what they became. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: This is a mention of those with me. He said: A hadith of those with me, and a hadith of those before me. And His statement: But most of them do not know the truth means: Rather, most of these polytheists do not know the truth in what they say, nor in what they do and leave, so they turn away from the truth out of ignorance of it and lack of understanding. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away from the Book of God.
21:25: God Almighty says: And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messenger to any nation except that We revealed to him that there is no deity in the heavens or the earth, worthy of worship except Me, so worship Me. He says: So devote your worship to Me, and single out Me for divinity. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.’ He said: The messengers were sent with sincerity and monotheism, and no action is accepted from them ((Abu Ja`far said: I think it was me who said)): until they say it and acknowledge it, and the laws differ in the Torah, there is a law, in the Gospel, and in the Qur’an, there is a law, lawful and unlawful. And all of this is about sincerity to God and monotheism towards Him.
21:26: God Almighty says: And these disbelievers in their Lord said: The Most Gracious has taken a son from among His angels. So He, the Most High, said, out of awe of what they said, and disavowing what they described Him with, glory be to Him, saying, glorifying Him from that: That is not from His description. Rather, they are honored servants. He says: The angels are not as these disbelievers from among the children of Adam described them, but they are honored servants. He says: God honored them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants. He said: The Jews said that God, the Blessed and Exalted, had intermarried with the jinn, and the angels were from them. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said, in refutation of them and in response to them: Rather, they are honored servants. And the angels are not as they said, rather they are servants whom God has honored with His worship. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ The Jews and groups of people said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, is a circumciser to the jinn, and the angels are from the jinn. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants. And His statement: They do not precede Him in speech, the Most High says: They do not speak except what their Lord commands them to do, and they do not know any action except by Him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: God said: They do not precede Him in speech, praising them, and they act by His command.
21:27: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.
21:28: God Almighty says: He knows what is before the angels, what they have not attained, what it is, and what they are saying and doing, and what is behind them: He says: and what has passed before today of what they left behind them of times and ages what they did in it, they said that all of that is counted for them and against them, nothing of that is hidden from Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saeed told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He knows what is before them and what is behind them, meaning: He knows what they have sent forward and what they have lost of their deeds. And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, meaning: The angels do not intercede except for him with whom God is pleased. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, meaning: those for whom He is pleased to bear witness that there is no god but God. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, except for him with whom He is pleased, he said: for the one with whom He is pleased. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased on the Day of Resurrection, and they are fearful of Him. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: And they will not intercede on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. And His statement, And they are fearful for fear of Him, means: And they are fearful for fear of God and for fear of His punishment that it will befall them. He says: They are wary of disobeying Him and going against His commands and prohibitions.
21:29: God Almighty says: And whoever among the angels says, ‘I am a god besides God,’ We will recompense him with Hell. He says: We will reward him for saying that with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers. He says: Just as We recompense whoever among the angels says, ‘I am a god besides God,’ with Hell, thus do We recompense everyone who wrongs himself, disbelieves in God and worships other than Him. It was said: This verse refers to Satan. Those who said that said: We only said that because none of the angels said: I am a god besides God except Him. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And whoever among them says, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Who among the angels says, I am a god besides Him, and no one said it except Iblis, who called for the worship of himself, so this was revealed about Iblis. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.” This verse was specifically for the enemy of God, Iblis, when he said what he said, may God curse him and make him a devil, and He said: “Then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. He said: It is specifically for Satan.
21:30: God Almighty says: Did not those who disbelieved in God look with the eyes of their hearts, so that they could see with them, and know that the heavens and the earth were joined together? He says: There was no hole in them, but rather they were stuck together. It is said from this: So-and-so mended the tear: if he tightened it, so he mends it, mending it, and from this it is said of the woman whose vagina is joined together: Ritaq, and the ritaq is singular, and it is from the description of the heavens and the earth, and it came after His saying they were because it is a source, like false speech, fasting, and breaking the fast. And his saying, So We split them apart, means: We split them apart and separated them. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of God’s description of the heavens and the earth as being joined together, how the joining was done, and in what sense it was split apart. Some of them said: What he meant by that is that the heavens and the earth were joined together, and God separated them with air. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity? meaning: joined together. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told us: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them?... the verse, he says: They were joined together, then He raised the heaven and placed the earth. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We parted them, Ibn Abbas used to say: They were joined together, then God parted them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We separated them. He said: Al-Hasan and Qatada used to say: They were together, then God separated them with air. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that the heavens were joined together in one layer, then God split them apart and made them seven heavens, and likewise the earth was also joined together, then He split it apart and made it seven earths. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted, And We joined them together, and We parted them from the earth six earths with them, so those are seven earths, and from the sky six heavens with them, so those are seven heavens with them, he said: And the earth and the sky were not touching each other. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And they joined them together, then We split them apart. He said: They split into seven heavens, one above the other, and seven earths, one below the other. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similar to the hadith of Muhammad Ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Asim. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, who said: I asked Abu Salih about his statement, They were joined together, then We separated them. He said: The earth was joined together and the heavens were joined together, so He separated seven heavens from the sky and seven earths from the earth. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: There was one heaven, then He split it apart, and made it seven heavens in two days, on Thursday and Friday. And it was called Friday because He gathered together the creation of the heavens and the earth in it, so that is when He says He created the heavens and the earth in six days al-A’raf 7:54 - Yunus 10:3 - Hud 11:7 - al-Hadid 57:4 He says: They were joined together, then We split them apart. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was that the heavens were closed and did not rain, and the earth was also closed and did not produce vegetation, so He split the heaven with rain and the earth with vegetation. Who said that? Hannad told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? He said: They were joined together, and nothing came out of them, so He split the heaven with rain and split the earth with plants. He said: And this is His statement, And the heaven with its paths, and the earth with its rifts. al-Tariq 86:11-12. Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me: My father told us, on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyyah, regarding His statement, Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? He said: The sky was joined together and did not rain, and the earth was joined together and did not produce vegetation, so He split the sky with rain, and split the earth with vegetation, and made from water every living thing. Will they not believe? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We parted them? He said: The heavens were joined together, from which no rain descended, and the earth was joined together, from which no vegetation grew, so God parted them, and sent down rain from the sky, and split the earth and brought forth its vegetation. He recited, “And We parted them and made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?” Others said: It was said, So We split them apart because the night was before the day, so the day split. Who said that? Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He created the night before the day, then He said: They were joined together, then We separated them. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity of rain and vegetation, then We split the heaven with rain and the earth with vegetation? We said that this is more correct in this regard because His statement, And We made from water every living thing, indicates this, and that He, may His praise be glorified, did not follow that with a description of water with this quality except with what preceded it of mentioning its causes. If someone were to say: If that is the case, then how is it said: Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were joined together, and that the rain only descends from the lowest heaven? It is said: That is disputed. Some people have said: It only descends from the seventh heaven. Others have said: From the fourth heaven. If that were also as you mentioned, that it descends from the lowest heaven, then his statement: that the heavens and the earth would not have been evidence of the opposite of what we have said, because it is not impossible to say the heavens and what is meant by them is one, so they are pluralized, because each piece of them is a heaven, just as it is said: a garment of rags, and a shirt of rags. If someone were to say: How was it said that the heavens and the earth were, since the heavens are a plural, and the rule for the feminine plural is that it is said in its little form were and in its much form were? It would be said: It was only said that way because they are two types, so the heavens are one type and the earth is another, and that is similar to the statement of Al-Aswad bin Ya’far: Fate and death both kill the losers, watching my blackness Both of them said, and he mentioned death and dying because I described that he meant both types, and I was informed about Abu Ubaidah Muammar bin Al-Muthanna, he said: Ghalib Al-Nafili recited to me for Al-Qatami: Did it not sadden you that the ties of Qais and Taghlib were severed? So he made the ropes of Qais, which are a plural, and the ropes of Taghlib, which are a plural of two. And His statement: And We made from water every living thing. God Almighty says: And We gave life with the water that We send down from the sky to every thing. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And We made from water every living thing. He said: Every living thing was created from water. If someone were to say: How did He single out every living thing by making it from water, and not from other things? You know that crops, plants, trees, and other things that have no life live with water, and are neither called living nor dead? It is said: Because there is nothing of that that does not have life and death, even though its meaning differs in that from the meaning of living things, in that there are no souls in them and that living things have souls. Therefore it was said: And We made from water every living thing. And His saying: Do they not believe? He says: Do they not believe in that, and acknowledge the divinity of the One who did that, and single Him out for worship?
21:31: God Almighty says: Have these disbelievers not also seen from Our proofs against them and against all Our creation, that We have placed on the earth firmly fixed mountains? And fixed mountains is the plural of fixed, which means firm. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We placed firm mountains on the earth, meaning mountains. And His saying, That it might not topple over with them, means that it might not topple over with them. God Almighty says: So We placed these firm mountains on this earth, and We made them steadfast so that it would not topple over with the people, and so that they would be able to stand firm on its back. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, he said: They were on the earth, it was shaking with them, it was not stable, then they woke up and God had made the mountains, which are the fixed mountains, pegs for the earth. And We placed therein paths, roads: meaning paths, the singular of which is faj. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We placed therein paths means landmarks. And his statement, paths means roads, which is the plural of path. Ibn Abbas, as reported from him, said: What he meant by his saying, And We placed therein paths, is that We placed therein the mountains. So the ha’ and the alif in his saying, And We placed therein are from the mention of the mountains. Al-Qasim told us that, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, his statement, And We placed therein paths, means roads, he said: between the mountains. Rather, we chose the other statement in that, and we made the ha’ and the alif from the mention of the earth, because if they were from its mention, then that would include the plain and the mountain, and that is because all of that is on the earth, and God has made for His creation in all of that paths and roads, and there is no indication that he meant by that the paths of some of the earth that He made for them paths, without some, so the generality of it is more appropriate. And His saying, Perhaps they will be guided, God Almighty says: We made these paths in the earth so that they may be guided to travel in them.
21:32: God Almighty says: And We made the sky a ceiling for the earth, elevated. His statement protected means: We protected it from every accursed devil. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a preserved ceiling, he said: raised. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We made the sky a protected ceiling the verse: a raised ceiling, and a restrained wave. And His statement, And they turn away from its signs, means: These polytheists turn away from the signs of the heavens, and by its signs He means its sun, moon, and stars. Turn away, means: They turn away from thinking about it, and pondering what is in it of God’s proofs against them, and its evidence of the oneness of its Creator, and that worship should only be for the One Who managed and made it, and it is only suitable for Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And they turn away from its signs. He said: The sun, the moon, and the stars are the signs of the heavens. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And His statement, And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit swimming, God Almighty says: And God is He who created for you, O people, the night and the day, as a blessing from Him upon you and an argument and proof of His great power, and that divinity belongs to Him and not to everything else, so they differ from you for the sake of your livelihood and the affairs of your worldly life and your afterlife. And He also created the sun and the moon, each in an orbit swimming, meaning: All of that is swimming in an orbit. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the ark that God mentioned in this verse. Some of them said: It is like the shape of an iron millstone. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Each in an orbit is swimming, he said: An orbit is like the shape of an iron millstone. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Everything is in an orbit. He said: An orbit is like the shape of a millstone. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Each one is swimming in an orbit. He said: The orbit of the sky. Others said: Rather, the sphere that God mentioned in this place is the speed of the sun, moon, stars, and other things. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Each in an orbit is swimming, the orbit is running and speed. Others said: Rather, it is the pole around which the stars revolve. The one who said this quote cited the words of the rajaz poet as evidence for his statement: She kept talking to the revolving universe until morning, when she started making her predictions. Others said about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Each in an orbit is swimming: meaning in the orbit of the sky. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Each one floats in an orbit. He said: It runs in the orbit of the sky as you saw. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Each in an orbit is swimming, he said: The orbit that is between the sky and the earth is from the courses of the stars, the sun, and the moon. And he recited, Blessed is He who has placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light. (al-Furqan 25:61) And he said: Those constellations are between the sky and the earth and are not on the earth. Each in an orbit is swimming, he said: In what is between the sky and the earth: the stars, the sun, and the moon. It was reported on the authority of Al-Hassan that he used to say: The ark is a mill like the spindle shaft. The correct thing to say about this is to say as God Almighty said: Each one floats in an orbit. It is possible that this orbit is, as Mujahid said, like the iron of a millstone, and as was mentioned by Al-Hasan like the millstone’s mill, and it is possible that it is a blocked wave, and that it is the pole of the sky, because the orbit in the speech of the Arabs is everything that revolves, so its plural is orbits. I mentioned the saying of the rajaz poet: She began to talk to the revolving universe Since everything that was mentioned in her speech, and there was no evidence in the Book of God, nor in a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor from anyone whose words are deemed an excuse, that it was from whomever it was, it is obligatory for us to say what he said about it, and to remain silent about what we have no knowledge of. Since the correct statement in this regard is what we have mentioned, then the interpretation of the statement is: The sun and the moon, all of that is in a circle, swimming. As for his saying, they swim, it means: they run. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Each in an orbit is swimming, he said: They run. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They glorify, he said: They run. And it was said, Each one swims in an orbit, so he made the report about the sun and the moon like the report about the children of Adam with the waw and the nun, and he did not say: They glorify or she glorifies, as it was said, And the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me (Yusuf 12:4) because prostration is from the actions of the children of Adam, so when the sun and the moon were described with actions similar to theirs, the report about them was made like the report about them.
21:33: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating.
21:34: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: We did not immortalize any of the children of Adam before you, O Muhammad, in this world so that We will immortalize you in it. You must die as Our messengers died before you. If you die, will they be the immortals? He says: So these polytheists who associate others with their Lord are the immortals in this world after you? No! That is not the case, rather they will die in any case, whether you live or die. So the letter fa was inserted in in and it is a condition, and in its response, because the condition is connected to the statement before it. It was also inserted in His statement understanding because it is a response to the condition. If there was no fa in His statement understanding, it would have been permissible in two ways: One of them is that it is deleted, and it is intended, and the other is that it is intended to be brought forward to the condition, so it is as if He said: Are they the immortals if I die? And His saying, Every soul will taste death, God Almighty says: Every soul created by Him will suffer the pangs of death and drink its cup. And His statement, And We test you with evil and with good as trial, God Almighty says: And We test you, O people, with evil, which is hardship, with which We test you, and with good, which is ease, abundance, and well-being, so We test you with it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, his statement, And We test you with evil and with good as trial, he said: with ease and hardship, and both are trials. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We test you with evil and with good as trial, meaning: We test you with evil as a trial and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned, he said: We test them with what they love and what they hate, we test them with that to see how grateful they are for what they love, and how patient they are for what they hate. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We test you with evil and with good, means: We test you with hardship and ease, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience, guidance and misguidance. And his statement, And to Us you will be returned, means: And to Us they will return and be rewarded for their deeds, good and bad.
21:35: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Every soul will taste death, and We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned.
21:36: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And when those who disbelieve in God see you, O Muhammad, they take you only in ridicule. He says: They take you only in mockery. Some of them say to each other: Is this the one who mentions your gods? I mean by his saying: He mentions your gods in a bad way and finds fault with them, out of astonishment at that. God Almighty says: They are amazed at your mention, O Muhammad, of their gods who do not harm or benefit with evil. And they remember the Most Gracious who created them and bestowed blessings upon them, from whom He benefited them, and in whose hand is their harm, and to Him is their return, as is appropriate for them to mention Him with it. They are disbelievers. The Arabs place mention in place of praise and blame, so they say: We heard so-and-so, meaning we heard him mention him in a bad way and find fault with him. An example of that is the saying of Antarah: Do not mention my dowry and what I fed him, lest your skin be like the skin of a mangy dog. He meant by that: Do not criticize my dowry, and we heard him mentioned in a good way.
21:37: God Almighty says: He created man meaning Adam from haste. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: He who hastens in his structure and creation, is hasty and in haste. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, He created man from haste, he said: When the soul was breathed into his knees, he went to get up, so God said, He created man from haste. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When the spirit was blown into him, meaning into Adam, and it entered his head, he sneezed, and the angels said: Say, Praise be to God, so he said: Praise be to God, so God said to him: May your Lord have mercy on you. When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise, and when it entered his stomach, he desired food, so he jumped up before the spirit reached his feet, in haste, to the fruits of Paradise. That is when He says, Man was created of haste, meaning: Man was created hasty. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Man was created from haste. He said: He was created in haste. Others said: Its meaning is: He created man in haste: that is, from the haste in God’s creation of him, from the speed in it, and in haste. And they said: God created him at the end of the day on Friday before sunset, in haste in His creation of him before its setting. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, He created man in haste, he said: The statement of Adam when he was created after everything else at the end of the day on the day of creation, and when the spirit revived his eyes, his tongue, and his head, and it had not yet reached his lower body, he said: O Lord, hasten my creation before sunset. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said: Man was created in haste. He said: Adam when he was created after everything, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said in his hadith: He hastened my creation, for the sun has set. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He created man in haste, he said: He created Adam in haste on the last day of those two days, meaning Friday, and He created him in haste, and made him hasty. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra who said something similar to this statement said: He only said: He created man in haste, meaning that He created him from hastening the matter, because He said, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is 16:40. He said: This is haste. And His statement, So do not be impatient, “I will show you My signs,” and according to the statement of the author of this statement, all of God’s creation must have been created in haste, because all of that was created by saying to it, Be, and it was. So if that is the case, then what is the reason for mentioning that man was created in haste, unlike all other things, and all of them were created in haste? And in God’s mentioning man in particular, there is clear evidence that the statement in that is not what the author of this statement said. Others among them said: This is from the inverted, and the calf was created from man, and the calf was created from man. They said that it is like his saying: Verily, its keys would be a burden for a company of strong men (al-Qasas 28:76). It is only so that a company of strong men would be burdened by it. They said: This and what is similar to it are common and well-known in the speech of the Arabs. They said: And the people spoke with what they understood. They said: That is like their saying: The she-camel appeared, and like their saying: When Sirius rises, and the lute rests on the chameleon: meaning the chameleon rests on the lute, like the poet’s saying: And ride horses that are relentless among them, and spears are torn apart by red spears. As Ibn Muqbil said: I lowered my hand over the robe, taking it individually, dragging it on the hands of the redeemers. He means: I pulled the garment off my hand, and something similar to that from the reversed. And in the consensus of the people of interpretation on the contrary to this statement, sufficiency is sufficient and does not require citing evidence of corruption from anything else. Abu Ja`far said: The correct interpretation of this, according to us, is what we mentioned from those who said that its meaning is: Man was created in haste in his creation, meaning in haste and speed in that. And it was said thus because his creation was preceded by sunset in the last hour of the day on Friday, and at that time the soul was breathed into him. We said that the first of the statements we mentioned about this is the most correct, because of the evidence of the Almighty’s saying, I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient. And Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Idris told us: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is an hour on Friday that is short. He said: No Muslim servant will ask God for good in it except that God will give it to him.” Abdullah ibn Salam said: I know what hour it is. It is the last hours of the day on Friday. God said: “Man was created in haste. I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient.” Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi, Abda bin Sulayman, and Aseer bin Amr told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, who said: Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. He mentioned the words of Abdullah bin Salam in a similar manner. The interpretation of the statement, if the correct interpretation of that is what we said, with what we cited as evidence, Man was created from haste, and therefore his Lord hastens the punishment, I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient. O you who are impatient with your Lord for the signs, who say to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Rather, he is a poet, so let him bring us a sign as the first ones sent My signs, as I showed them to the nations before you whom We destroyed for their denial of the messengers when the signs came to them, so do not be impatient. He says: So do not impatient your Lord, for We will bring them to you and show them to you. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, He created man from haste. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it, He created man from haste, with a damma on the kha’, according to the doctrine of what is not named by the agent. Hamid al-A’raj read it, He created with a fatha on the kha’, meaning: God created man. The reading that the reciters of the regions follow is the reading that I do not permit to differ from. And His statement, And they say, ‘When will this promise come, if you should be truthful?’ God Almighty says: And these people who are impatient for the signs and the punishment say to their Lord, may God bless him and grant him peace: When will this promise come to us? He says: When will this punishment that you promise us come to us, if you are truthful in what you promise us of that? It was said: This is the promise and the promised meaning, so that the listeners will know its meaning. It was said: If you should be truthful as if they said that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him. And when is in the accusative case, because its meaning is: What time is this promise, and what day is it, so it is in the accusative case as a circumstance because it is a time.
21:38: Interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’
21:39: God Almighty says: If these unbelievers who are hastening the punishment of their Lord knew what a trial they would be in when the Fire scorches their faces, and they are therein gloomy, and they cannot keep the Fire from scorching their faces, nor from their backs to repel it with their own hands. Nor will they be helped. He says: Nor will they have a helper to help them, who will rescue them then from the punishment of God, they would not have remained in the state they are remaining in of disbelief in God, and they would have hastened to repent from it and believe in God, and they would not have hastened the trial for themselves.
21:40: God Almighty says: This fire that scorches the faces of these disbelievers whose situation is described in this Surah will not come when it comes to them with their knowledge of its time, but it will come to them suddenly, without them feeling its coming, and it will confuse them. He says: It will suddenly overwhelm them, and scorch their faces in plain sight, like a man who is confounded by something in his face, until the one who is confounded remains as if he is bewildered by it. And they will not be able to repel it, He says: So they will not be able to repel it when it surprises them, so it will confuse them, nor will they be able to wait, He says: Nor will they, even if they are not able to repel it from themselves, delay the punishment with it for a repentance they will utter, and a return they will turn back, because it is not a time of action and an hour of repentance and return, but rather it is an hour of recompense and reward.
