21:41: God the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If these people who say to you: Is this anything but a human being like you? Do you then practice magic while you see? When they see you, they mock and say: This is the one who mentions your gods. It is disbelief on their part in God and an audacity towards Him. Indeed, messengers of Our messengers whom We sent before you to their nations were mocked. He says: So it became necessary and what they mocked of their nations befell those who mocked them and ridiculed them. He says: What they mocked of the affliction and torment that their messengers used to warn them would befall them befell them. They mock: He says: So these mockers of you from these disbelievers will not go beyond being like their predecessors from the nations that denied their messengers. So the punishment and wrath of God will befall them because of their mockery of you, similar to what befell them.
21:42: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who hasten you with the punishment, who say: When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful: Who will protect you, O people? Who will guard you and watch over you at night when you sleep, and during the day when you act, from the Most Gracious? He says: From the command of the Most Gracious if it descends upon you, and from His punishment if it befalls you. And he left out mentioning the command, and it was said from the Most Gracious, daring to make the listeners know who mentioned it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement: “Say: Who guards you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?” He said: He guards you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “Say: Who guards you by night and by day from the Most Gracious?” Say: Who guards you by night and by day from the Most Gracious? It is said from this: I guarded the al-Nas 114:if I guarded them, I protected them, as Ibn Harmah said: Salma, may God protect her, was stingy with something that would have caused her misery. His saying: Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord. His saying: Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord. This is a confirmation of a denial that those addressed by these words have recognized, even if it is not mentioned in this place apparently. The meaning of the words is: Why should they not know that they have no protector from the command of God when it befalls them by night or by day? Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord’s admonitions and His proofs with which He has argued against them. They do not ponder that, so they do not consider it, out of their ignorance and foolishness.
21:43: God the Most High says: Do these people who hasten their Lord to punish have gods who can protect them if We inflict Our punishment on them and send down Our might on them instead of Us? Its meaning is: Or do they have gods other than Us who can protect them from Us? Then God the Most High described the gods as weak and humiliated, and that is their description, so He said: How can their gods whom they call upon instead of Us protect them from Us when they cannot help themselves? And His statement: Nor can they accompany Us The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that, and regarding the meaning of accompanying, so some of them said: He meant by that the gods, and that they do not accompany with good from God. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They cannot help themselves. He means the gods. Nor do they accompany Us. He says: They do not accompany with good from God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Nor will they be helped by us. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Abu Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Nor will they be companions of us. He said: They will not be aided. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? to His saying: who accompany he said: who are aided, he said: Mujahid said: Nor are they protected. Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: nor do they accompany us means they are not neighbors. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: nor do they have any companions from us means: nor do they have any protection from us, and this is his statement: And he protects, but no protection is given to him (al-Mu’minun 23:88) meaning the companion, which is the person who has a guard from what he fears, so this is his statement: they have any companions. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: This is the saying that we have narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, and that they is from his saying nor they from the mention of the infidels, and that his saying: they accompany means: they are neighbors, they accompany by neighboring, because it was said of the Arabs: I am your neighbor from so-and-so and companion, meaning: I protect you and I protect you, and if they are not accompanied by neighboring and there is no one to protect them from the punishment of God with God’s wrath upon them, then they are not accompanied by good and they are not aided.
21:44: God Almighty says: These polytheists have no gods to protect them from Us, nor any protector to protect them from Our punishment, when We intend to punish them, and they rely on that, and they disobey Our messengers, relying on that. But We gave them enjoyment in this worldly life, and their fathers before them, until life was prolonged for them, and they remained in their disbelief. No admonition of punishment came to them from Us, nor a deterrent of retribution for their disbelief and disobedience to Our command, and their worship of idols and statues. So they forgot Our covenant and were ignorant of the place of Our blessing upon them, and they did not know the place of gratitude. And His statement: Do they not see that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? God Almighty says: Do these polytheists who ask about the signs and hasten the punishment not see that We come to the land and destroy it from its sides by subduing its people, overpowering them, expelling them from it and killing them with swords, so that they may consider that and learn from it, and beware of us bringing down from our punishment upon them what we brought down upon those to whom we did that from the people of the borders? The mention of those who say this and those who oppose it has come before, with the narrations from them in Surat Ar-Ra`d, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement: Understand the victors. The Most High says: Are these polytheists who hasten Muhammad’s punishment the ones who will overcome Us, while they have seen Our subjugation of the one in whose courtyard We have brought Our might to the ends of the earth? That is not the case, rather We are the ones who will prevail. Rather, this is a rebuke from God the Most High to these polytheists for their ignorance. He says: Do they think that they will overcome Muhammad and subjugate him, while He has subjugated those who opposed him from the ends of the earth other than them? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Understand the victors means they are not victorious, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the victor.
21:45: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these speakers: Let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent: I only warn you, O people, by the revelation of God which He reveals to those with Him, and I frighten you with His punishment. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “Say: I only warn you by revelation” meaning by this Qur’an. His saying: And the deaf do not hear the call. The reciters differed on that, because its parts are generally recited by the reciters of the regions. And and you do not hear with the opening of the ya from yasma’ means that it is a verb for the deaf, and the deaf are in this case in the nominative case. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami that he used to recite and you do not hear with the ta and with a damma on it, so the deaf according to this recitation are in the nominative case, because his saying and you do not hear did not name its agent, and its meaning according to this recitation is: And God does not hear the deaf’s call. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in our view is what the reciters of the regions have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this. The meaning of this is: The disbeliever in God should not listen with the hearing of his heart to the remembrance of what is in God’s revelation of admonitions and remembrance, so that he may remember and consider it, and thus be deterred from the misguidance he is in if it is recited to him. What is meant by this is: But he turns away from considering it and thinking about it, like the deaf person who does not hear what is said to him and does not act upon it. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned. He said: The disbeliever has become deaf to the Book of God, he does not hear it, nor does he benefit from it, nor does he understand it, just as the believer and the people of faith hear it.
21:46: God Almighty says: And if these hasteners of punishment, O Muhammad, were touched by a whiff of the punishment of your Lord, meaning by whiff the share and portion, from their saying: So-and-so gave so-and-so a share of his gift: if he gave him a portion or share of the money. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And if a blast of the punishment of your Lord touches them... the verse, he says: If a punishment befalls them. And His statement: They will surely say, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ He says: If this breath of punishment from your Lord befalls them, O Muhammad, for their denial of you and their disbelief, then they will know at that time the consequences of their denial of you, and they will acknowledge against themselves the grace and kindness of God to them, and their ingratitude for His favors toward them, and they will say, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers in our worship of gods and rivals, and we abandoned the worship of God who created us and bestowed favors upon us, and we placed worship in the wrong place.
21:47: God the Almighty says: And We shall set up the scales Justice is fairness, and He made justice, which is a singular noun, from the description of the scales, and it is a plural because in the doctrine of justice, satisfaction, and consideration. And His saying: For the Day of Resurrection means: For the people of the Day of Resurrection, and whoever of His creation comes to God on that day. Some of the Arabists directed the meaning of that to fi as if its meaning to him is: And We shall set up the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: So no soul shall be wronged in the least means: So God shall not wrong a soul of those who come to Him in the least by punishing him for a sin he did not commit or depriving him of the reward of an action he did, or an act of obedience with which he obeyed Him, but He rewards the doer of good for his good, and He does not punish the wrongdoer except for his wrongdoing. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saeed told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection… to the end of the verse, and it is like his statement: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth (al-A’raf 7:8). He means by the weighing: justice between them with the truth in good and bad deeds. So whoever’s good deeds surround his bad deeds, his scales will be heavy, meaning: his good deeds will take away his bad deeds. And whoever’s bad deeds surround his good deeds, his scales will be light, and his mother will be in the abyss, meaning: his bad deeds will take away his good deeds. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, he said: It is only an example, just as weight is permissible, so is truth permissible. Al-Thawri said: Layth said on the authority of Mujahid, And We will set up the just scales, he said: Justice. And His statement, And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, means: And if what he has of good deeds, or upon him of bad deeds is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it: He says: We will bring it and bring it to him. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, he said: It will be brought to you and against you, then He will pardon if He wills or take it, and He will reward for what He has done of obedience. And Mujahid used to say about that what: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, he said: We will reward it. Amr ibn Abdul Hamid narrated: Sufyan narrated from Laith from Mujahid that he used to say: And if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, he said: We will reward it, and he said: We will bring it forth, so he used his statement it as a feminine metaphor. Even though what preceded that was his statement the weight of a mustard seed, because he meant by his statement it the seed, not the mithqal. If he meant the mithqal, it would have been said that way. It has been mentioned that Mujahid interpreted his statement: We will bring it forth as we mentioned from him, because he used to read that as We will bring it forth with an extended alif. And his statement: And sufficient are We as reckoners, he said: And it is sufficient for those who witnessed that situation to be reckoners, because no one is more knowledgeable about their deeds and what preceded them in this world, good or bad, than us.
21:48: God Almighty says: And We gave Moses, son of Imran, and his brother Aaron the Criterion, meaning the book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and that is the Torah according to some of them. Mention of who said: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The Criterion: he said: the Book. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion. The Criterion is the Torah, its lawful and unlawful things, and what God distinguished between truth and falsehood with. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion, that the Criterion is the truth that God gave to Moses and Aaron, He distinguished between them and Pharaoh, He judged between them with justice. And he recited, And We did not send down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion (al-Anfal 8:41), that is, the Day of Badr. Abu Ja`far said: This statement that Ibn Zayd said about that is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, because of the inclusion of the waw in the light. If the Criterion was the Torah, as the one who said that said, then the revelation would have been: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, a light. Because the light that God gave Moses and Aaron is the Torah, which illuminated for them and for those who followed them the matter of their religion, and made them see what is lawful and what is unlawful. And He did not mean by that in this place the light of the eyes. And the inclusion of the waw in that is evidence that the Criterion is not the Torah, which is a light. If someone were to say: What is wrong with the fact that light is an attribute of the Criterion, even if there is a waw in it, and its meaning is: And light We gave him that, as He said: With the adornment of the stars * And protection 37:6? It would be said to him: Even though the speech allows for that, the most common of its meanings is what we have said. And it is obligatory to direct the meanings of the speech of God to the most common and well-known of its aspects known to the Arabs, unless there is something to the contrary that must be accepted from a proof from the report or reason. And His saying: And a reminder for the righteous, meaning: And a reminder for those who fear God by obeying Him, performing His duties, and avoiding His disobedience, He reminded them of what He gave Moses and Aaron of the Torah.
21:49: God Almighty says: We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion: the Reminder which We gave them is for the righteous who fear their Lord unseen, meaning in this world, lest He punish them in the Hereafter if they come before Him by neglecting what He has obligated them to do of His obligations. They are out of fear of Him, they maintain His limits and obligations, and they are fearful of the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place, wary that it will come upon them, and they will return to their Lord having neglected what is obligatory upon them for God, so He will punish them with a punishment that they cannot bear.
21:50: God, the Most High, says: This Qur’an that We sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a reminder for those who remember it, and an admonition for those who take heed. Blessed is We that We have sent it down, just as We sent down the Torah to Moses and Aaron, a reminder for the righteous. Then will you deny it? God, the Most High, says: Then will you, O people, deny this Book that We sent down to Muhammad and say, ‘Rather, they said, “Confused dreams. Rather, he invented it. Rather, he is a poet. So let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent.” (Al-Anbiya’: 5). Rather, what We gave him of that is a reminder for the righteous, like what We gave Moses and Aaron, a reminder for the righteous. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And this is a blessed reminder... to his statement: Then will you deny it?: meaning this Qur’an.
21:51: God Almighty says: And We had already given Abraham his sound judgment before Moses and Aaron, and guided him to the truth, and saved him from among his people and his family from the worship of idols, just as We did that with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with Abraham, so We saved him from his people and his clan from the worship of idols, and guided him to the path of sound judgment as a success from Us for him. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And We had already given Abraham his sound judgment before, he said: We guided him when he was young. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And We had already given Abraham his sound judgment before. He said: We guided him when he was young. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: We gave Abraham his sound judgment before, he said: We guided him when he was young. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We had already given Abraham his sound judgment before, meaning: We gave him His guidance. And His statement: And We were knowing of him means: And We were knowing of him that he had certainty and faith in God and monotheism of Him, and did not associate anything with Him. When he said to his father and his people meaning at the time it was said to him and when it was said to them: What are these statues to which you are devoted? He says: He said to them: What are these images to which you are devoted! And those statues were their idols that they used to worship. Muhammad bin Amr also told me, and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: What are these statues to which you are devoted? He said: The idols. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And we have previously explained in this book of ours that the one who is devoted to something is the one who resides in it with evidence for that, and we mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation.
21:52: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: When he said to his father and his people, ‘What are these statues to which you are devoted?’
21:53: God Almighty says: The father of Abraham and his people said to Abraham: We found our fathers worshipping these idols, so we follow the religion of our fathers, worshipping them as they used to worship. Abraham said: You were, O people, you and your fathers, in your worship of them, in manifest error. He says: In going astray from the path of truth, and clearly deviating from the right path. He says: It is clear to whoever contemplates it with reason, that you are also in deviance from the truth. They said: Have you brought us the truth? He says: His father and his people said to him: Have you brought us the truth in what you say? Or are you, a playful jester, one of the players?
21:54: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘You and your fathers were in manifest error.’
21:55: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the players?’
21:56: God Almighty says: Abraham said to them: Rather, I have come to you with the truth, not to play, and your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I agree with you that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, not the statues to which you are devoted, and not everyone other than Him is a witness among the witnesses, saying: So worship Him, not these statues which are His creation that do not harm or benefit.
21:57: It was mentioned that Abraham, peace be upon him, swore this oath in secret from his people, and that no one heard it from him except the one who revealed it to him when they said: Whoever did this to our gods is indeed among the wrongdoers. They said: We heard a young man mentioning them called Abraham. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And by God, I will surely destroy your idols, he said: The statement of Abraham when his people asked him to follow them to a festival of theirs, but he refused and said: I am sick, and a man from among them heard him threatening their idols and stayed behind, and he is the one who says, We heard a young man mentioning them, whose name was Abraham (Al-Anbiya’: 60). Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And by God, I will surely destroy your idols, he said: We think that he said that when they did not hear him after they had turned their backs. And his saying: So He made them into fragments, except for one of their greatest ones. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A’mash, and Al-Kisa’i, recited it as So He made them into fragments... meaning all of them, as if they intended by it the plural of Jadhdh and Jadhdh, just as the light is pluralized as khafaaf, and the generous is karram. The first of the two readings in this regard, in our opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it as jazadhan with a damma on the jim, due to the consensus of the readers of the regions on it, and that what they agreed upon is correct. If it is read in this way, it is a verbal noun like rafat, “al-fatat,” and al-daqqaq, not a singular one. As for the one who reads it with a kasra on the jim, then it is the plural of al-jadhdh, and al-jadhdh is a verbal noun derived from majdhudhu ilayh, like kasir and hashim, and al-majdhudha is the one that is broken in pieces. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So He made them into fragments, meaning: debris. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Jathadh is like stubble. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then He made them into fragments: meaning pieces. The reason why Abraham, peace be upon him, did that to the gods of his people was: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, that Ibrahim’s father said to him: O Ibrahim, we have a festival. If you would go out with us to it, our religion would please you. So when it was the day of the festival, they went out to it, Ibrahim went out with them, and when he was part of the way, he threw himself down and said: I am sick, he said: My foot is ailing. So they pressed his feet together and he was lying dead. So when they had gone, he called out to the last of them, and twice the number of people remained: By God, I will surely destroy your idols after you have turned and departed. So they heard him say it. Then Ibrahim returned to the house of the gods, and if they were in a great hall, facing the door of the hall, a great idol, next to it, smaller than it, each idol next to it smaller than it, until they reached the door of the hall, and if they had prepared food, they would place it in front of the gods. They said: When it is time for us to return, we will return, and the gods have blessed our food, so we ate. So when Ibrahim looked at them and at the food in front of them, he said: Will you not eat? (al-Dhariyat 51:27) When they did not answer him, he said, What is the matter with you that you do not speak? He finished striking them with his right hand. (al-Saffat 37:92) So he took an iron axe, and he made gouges in each idol on its edges, then he hung the axe around the neck of the largest idol, then he left. When the people came to their food, they looked at their gods. They said, ‘Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is one of the wrongdoers.’ They said, ‘We heard a young man mentioning them, whose name was Abraham.’ And his saying, Except for a great one of theirs, means: Except for a great one of the gods, for Abraham did not break it, but rather, as he mentioned, he hung the axe around its neck. In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Except for their greatest. Ibn Abbas said: Except for their greatest, the greatest of their gods. Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said: And Abraham placed the axe with which he destroyed their idols leaning against the chest of their greatest, which he left. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: He turned to them as God Almighty said: Strike with the right hand 37:93. Then he began to break them with an axe in his hand, until the largest idol remained. He tied the axe to his hand, then left them. When his people returned, they saw what he had done to their idols. This terrified them and they were greatly shocked by it and said: Whoever did this to our gods is indeed among the wrongdoers. And His statement: Perhaps to Him they will return means: Abraham did that to their gods so that they would take heed and know that if she did not repel from herself what Abraham did to her, then she would be further from repelling from others those who wanted to harm them, so they would return from what they were doing of worshipping her to what he was doing of his religion and the oneness of God, and disavowal of idols. In a similar vein, the commentators said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Perhaps they will return to Him. He said: He tempted them with that so that perhaps they would remember or see.
21:58: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So He made them into fragments, except for their biggest one, that perhaps they would return to it.
21:59: God Almighty says: The people of Abraham said when they saw their gods cut off, except for the one to whom Abraham tied the axe: Who did this to our gods? Indeed, he who did this to our gods is among the wrongdoers: that is, among those who do to them what he had no right to do. They said, ‘We heard a young man mentioning them, whose name was Abraham.’ He says: Those who heard him say, By God, I will surely destroy your idols after you have turned and departed. We heard a young man mentioning them with a fault, whose name was Abraham. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, They said we heard a young man mentioning them. Ibn Jurayj said: He mentions them and criticizes them. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, his saying, We heard a young man mentioning them, whose name was Ibrahim. We heard him insulting her, criticizing her, and mocking her. We did not hear anyone say that except him, and he is the one who we think did this to her. And His statement, Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may bear witness, God Almighty says: The people of Abraham said to one another: Then bring him who did this to our gods, whom you heard mentioning them with a defect, cursing them and slandering them before the eyes of the people. It was said that the meaning of that is: before the heads of the people. Some of them said that its meaning is: before the eyes of the people and in their sight. They said that what he means by that is to reveal the one who did that to the people, as the Arabs say when a matter becomes apparent and famous: That was before the eyes of the people, meaning that it was in the hands of the people. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement, Perhaps they will bear witness. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Perhaps people will bear witness against him, that he is the one who did that, so their testimony against him will be proof for us against him. They said: They only did that because they hated to take him without intention. Who said that? Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, “They said: Bring him before the eyes of the people, perhaps they will testify” that he did that. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And bring it before the eyes of the people that they may bear witness, he said: They hated to take it without intention. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Perhaps they will witness what they are being punished with, so they will see it and witness it. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When report of what Abraham had done to the gods of his people reached Nimrod and the nobles of his people, they said: Bring him before the eyes of the people, perhaps they will witness - meaning what was being done to him. The most obvious meaning of that is that they said: Bring him before the eyes of the people, perhaps they will witness our punishment of him, because if what was meant by that was for them to witness his action, it would have been said: Look who witnessed him doing that, and it would not have been said: Bring him before the people.
21:60: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘We heard a young man mention them, whose name is Ibrahim.’
21:61: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Bring him before the eyes of the people, perhaps they will bear witness.’
21:62: God Almighty says: So they brought Abraham, and when they brought him they said to him: Did you do this to our gods by breaking them, O Abraham? Abraham answered them: Rather, their greatest and most important one did it, so ask the gods who did this to them and broke them if they speak for themselves. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When he was brought to him and his people gathered around him before their king Nimrod, they said: Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham? He said: Rather, their greatest one did it, so ask them, if they should speak. He was angry that they should worship these little ones with him while he was greater than them, so he broke them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Rather, their chief did it... the verse, and it is this characteristic with which he deceived them. Some of those who do not believe in the narrations and do not accept from the report anything except what is widely transmitted from the common people, have claimed that the meaning of his statement, Rather, this their leader did it, is: Rather, this their leader did it. If they can speak, then ask them. That is, if the broken gods can speak, then their leader is the one who broke them. This statement is contrary to what the narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown, that Abraham only told three lies, all about God: his statement, Rather, this their leader did it, his statement, I am ill 37:89, and his statement to Sarah, She is my sister. It is not impossible that God, the Most High, permitted His friend to do that, so that he could accuse his people of it, and use it as evidence against them, and make them aware of their mistake and their poor view of themselves, just as Joseph’s muezzin said to his brothers, O caravan, you are thieves 37:70, and they had not stolen anything.
21:63: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Rather, their chief did it, so ask them, if they should speak.’
21:64: God Almighty says: So they remembered when Abraham, peace be upon him, said to them, Rather, their chief did it, so ask them, if they should speak, in their minds, and they returned to their minds, and some of them looked at each other, and they said, "You people are wrongdoers, this man, in your questioning of him, and your saying to him: Who did this to our gods, O Abraham? And these are your gods to whom he did what he did to your city, so ask them." And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: “So they returned to themselves and said: ‘Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.’” He said: They were afraid and returned from him, meaning from Abraham, regarding what they had claimed against him of breaking them, to themselves among themselves, and they said: We have wronged him, and we do not see him except as he said. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: So they returned to themselves, he said: They looked at each other, “and said: ‘Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.’” And His saying, Then they lowered their heads, God Almighty says: Then they were defeated in the argument, so they argued with Abraham with what was an argument for Abraham against them, and they said: You have certainly known that these idols do not speak. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then they said, meaning the people of Abraham, and they knew that they, meaning their gods, neither harm nor benefit nor strike, Indeed you know that these do not speak. That is, they do not speak, so tell us who did this to them, and they do not strike with hands, so we believe you. God says, Then they turned their heads upside down, in the argument against them for Abraham when he argued with them, so Abraham said at that time when the argument became clear to them with their saying, Indeed you know that these do not speak. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said: Then they lowered their heads. People were overcome by a state of terrible confusion. Others said: The meaning of this is: Then they relapsed in the sedition. Who said that? Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Then they lowered their heads. He said: They lowered their heads in the trial, and they said: You know that these do not speak. Some Arab scholars said: The meaning of this is: Then they turned back from what they knew of Abraham’s argument, and said: You have certainly known that these people do not speak. We have chosen the statement that we have said about the meaning of that, because turning something upside down means turning it on its head, and making its top its bottom. It is known that the people did not accept it on their own heads, and that their argument was turned upside down, so the report about them was established in place of the report about their argument. Since that was the case, then turning upside down the argument is undoubtedly the argument of the one arguing against his opponent, with what is an argument for his opponent. As for the statement of al-Suddi: Then they turned upside down in the tribulation, then they had not come out of the tribulation before that, so they turned upside down in it. As for the statement of the one who said from the people of Arabic what we mentioned about him, then it is a statement far from the concept. Do not ask them, but we ask you, so tell us who did that to them, and we have heard that you did that, but they were truthful in what they said, so they said, You have certainly known that these do not speak, and that is not a return from what they knew, but rather it is an admission of it.
21:65: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Then they lowered their heads. You have certainly known that these do not speak.”
21:66: God Almighty says: Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:Do you worship the most beautiful of people, something that can neither benefit you nor harm you, while you know that she could not prevent herself from those who wanted to harm her, nor could she speak if asked about those who did her harm, so she could tell about it. Are you not ashamed to worship something that is like this? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, “He said: ‘Do you then worship besides God that which can neither benefit you nor harm you?’” The verse. He said, may God have mercy on him: Do you not see that they did not repel the harm that befell them from themselves, and that they do not speak and tell you who did it to you, so how can they benefit you or harm you? And His saying, Fie upon you, means: Shame on you and on the gods that you worship besides God. Do you not understand the ugliness of what you do by worshipping that which neither harms nor benefits, so that you abandon its worship and worship God, who created the heavens and the earth, and in whose hand is benefit and harm.
21:67: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Fie upon you and upon what you worship besides God. Will you not then reason?”
21:68: God Almighty says: Some of Abraham's people said to each other: Burn Abraham with fire. And support your gods, if you are going to do so. He says: If you are going to support them, and do not want to stop worshipping them. It was said that the one who said that was a man from the Kurds of Persia. Mention who said that. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Burn him and support your gods, he said: It was said by a man from the Bedouins of Persia, meaning the Kurds. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Wahb bin Sulayman told me, on the authority of Shu`ayb al-Jubba`i, he said: The one who said, Burn him, was Haizan, so God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Nimrod and his people gathered around Abraham and said: Burn him and support your gods if you must do so. That is, you will not support them from him except by burning him with fire if you are going to support them. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Dinar, on the authority of Laith ibn Abi Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I recited this verse to Abdullah ibn Umar, and he said: Do you know, O Mujahid, who suggested that Abraham be burned in the fire? I said: No. He said: A man from the Bedouins of Persia. I said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do the Persians have Bedouins? He said: Yes, the Kurds are Bedouins of Persia, and a man from among them is the one who suggested that Abraham be burned in the fire. And his saying, “We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham,’” is omitted in the speech, and the evidence of what was mentioned about it was sufficient, which is: So they lit a fire for him to burn him, then they threw him into it, so We said to the fire: O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham. And it was mentioned that when they wanted to burn him, they built a structure for him as: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: “They said: ‘Build for him a building and throw him into the Fire’” 37:97. He said: So they confined him to a house and gathered firewood for him, until a woman would fall ill and say: ‘If God cures me, I will gather firewood for Abraham.’ So when they gathered firewood for him and gathered so much that the birds would pass by it and be burned by the intensity of its blazing, they went to him and raised him on top of the building. Abraham, peace be upon him, raised his head to the sky, and the sky, the earth, the mountains and the angels said: ‘Our Lord, Abraham is being burned for You.’ He said: ‘I know him better, and if he calls upon you, help him.’ Abraham said when he raised his head to the sky: ‘O God, You are the One in the heavens, and I am the One on the earth. There is no one on the earth who worships You except me. God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ So they threw him into the Fire, and he called out to it and said: ‘O Fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.’ So Gabriel, peace be upon him, was the one. Who called her. Ibn Abbas said: If her coldness had not been followed by peace, Abraham would have died from the severity of her coldness. On that day, there was no fire on earth that was not extinguished. She thought that it was her that was meant. When the fire was extinguished, they looked at Abraham, and behold, he was another man with him, and Abraham’s head was in his lap, wiping the sweat from his face. He mentioned that that man was the Angel of Shadow, and God sent down fire, and the children of Adam benefited from it. They brought Abraham out and brought him to the king, and he had not entered upon him before that. Ibrahim bin Al-Muqaddam Abu Al-Ash’ath told me, he said: Al-Mu’tamir told us, he said: I heard my father, he said: Qatada told us, on the authority of Abu Sulayman, on the authority of Ka’b, he said: The fire did not burn anything of Ibrahim except his bonds. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.’ He said: It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: No one benefited from it that day among the people, and Ka’b used to say: The fire burned nothing that day except his bonds. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, “O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham,” he said: It cooled him until it almost killed him, until it was said: And peace, he said: It does not harm him. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, he said: Ibrahim, the friend of God, said: I have never been in more comfortable days than the days I was in the Fire. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: When Abraham, the friend of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was thrown into the fire, the king, the keeper of the rain, said: O Lord, your friend Abraham, hoping that he would be given permission to send rain. He said: So God’s command was faster than that, and He said: “O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.” So there was no fire on earth that was not extinguished. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The best thing that Abu Ibrahim said when the plate was lifted from him while he was in the fire was that he found his forehead dripping with sweat, so he said at that time: What a good Lord your Lord is, O Ibrahim. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Wahb ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Shu`ayb al-Jubba`i, he said: Abraham was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old, and Isaac was slaughtered when he was seven years old, and Sarah gave birth to him when she was ninety years old, and his altar was two miles from the house of Elijah, and when Sarah learned what he had intended for Isaac, she remained silent for two days, and she died on the third day. Ibn Jurayj said: Ka`b al-Ahbar said: The fire did not burn anything of Abraham except the bonds with which they bound him. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muammar bin Sulayman Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of some of his companions, he said: Gabriel came to Abraham, peace be upon them both, while he was being bound or swaddled to be thrown into the fire. He said: O Abraham, do you have a need? He said: As for you, no. He said: Mu'tamir told us, he said: Ibn Ka'b told us, on the authority of Arqam, that Abraham said when they began to tie him up to throw him into the fire: There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds, to You is praise, and to You is dominion, You have no partner. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: “We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.’” He said: Peace does not harm him with its coldness, and if he had not said: “and peace,” the cold would have been more severe for him than the heat. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying cool he said: I cooled him down, “and peace” does not harm him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: “O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.” Ka’b said: No one on earth benefited from fire on that day, nor did fire burn anything on that day except the bonds of Abraham. Qatada said: No creature came that day except that it extinguished the fire for him, except for the gecko. Al-Zuhri said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his killing and called him Fuwaisaq. And His statement, And they intended to plot against him, God Almighty says: And they intended to plot against Abraham, so We made them the greatest losers, meaning the ones who perished. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And they intended a plot against him, but We made them the greatest losers. He said: They threw an old man from among them into the fire so that they could save him, just as Abraham, peace be upon him, was saved, and he was burned.
21:69: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.’
21:70: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they intended a plot against him, but We made them the greatest losers.
21:71: God Almighty says: And We saved Abraham and Lot from their enemies, Nimrod and his people, from the land of Iraq to the land which We have blessed for the worlds, which is the land of Ash-Sham. So he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, left his people and their religion and migrated to Ash-Sham. This story that God related of the report of Abraham and his people is a reminder from Him to the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Quraysh, that they had followed in their worship of idols, and that they had harmed Muhammad because of his prohibition of their worship. He called them to worship God, sincerely devoting their religion to Him, the way of the enemies of their father Abraham, and their opposition to his religion. And that Muhammad, in his innocence of worshipping them, and his sincere worship of God, and in calling them to innocence of idols, and in his patience with what he encounters from them in that, is following the path of his father Abraham, and that he is his expeller from among them, just as he expelled Abraham from among his people when they persisted in their error to his migration from the land of Ash-Sham. And with that he comforted his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the harm and suffering he encounters from his people, and taught him that he is his savior from them just as he saved his father Abraham from the disbelief of his people. The people of interpretation differed regarding the land to which God mentioned that He saved Abraham and Lot, and described that He blessed it for the worlds. Some of them said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Husayn bin Harith Al-Marwazi Abu Ammar told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abu bin Ka’b: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds. He said: Ash-Sham, and there is no fresh water except that it came out of that rock in the Holy House. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, to the land which We have blessed for the worlds, he said: Ash-Sham. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We saved him and Lot to the land which We have blessed for the worlds, they were in the land of Iraq, then they were saved to the land of Ash-Sham, and Ash-Sham was called the pillar of the abode of migration, and whatever was missing from the land was added to Ash-Sham, and whatever was missing from Ash-Sham was added to Palestine, and it was said: It is the land of the gathering and the resurrection, and in it the people will gather, and in it Jesus, son of Mary, will descend, and in it God will destroy the Sheikh of misguidance, the liar, the Antichrist. Abu Qilabah told us: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw in a dream that the angels carried the pillar of the Book and placed it in the Levant. I interpreted it to mean that when the tribulations occur, faith will be in the Levant.” He told us, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day in a sermon: ‘There will be an army in the Levant, an army in Iraq, and an army in Yemen.’ A man said, ‘O Messenger of God, choose for me.’ He said, ‘Go to the Levant, for God has guaranteed me the Levant and its people. Whoever refuses, let him go to its security and let him drink according to his capacity.’” It was mentioned to us that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: O Kaab, why don’t you move to Medina, for it is the place where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated and the place of his grave? So Kaab said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, I find in the revealed Book of God that Ash-Sham is God’s treasure from His land, and in it is His treasure from His servants. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds. He said: They both migrated from Kufa to Ash-Sham. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Abraham and Lot set out towards the Levant, and Abraham met Sarah, the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticized her people for their religion, so he married her on the condition that he would not change her. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Abraham went out as a migrant to his Lord, and Lot went out with him as a migrant, and he married Sarah, his cousin, and he went out with her seeking to escape with his religion, and safety in the worship of his Lord, until he settled in Harran, and he stayed there as long as God willed him to stay, then he left it as a migrant until he arrived in Egypt, then he left Egypt for the Levant, and he settled in the Seven Lands of Palestine, which is the wilderness of the Levant, and he settled in Al-Mu’tafikah, which is from the Seven Lands a day and a night’s journey away, or closer than that, so God sent him as a prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds, he said: He saved him from the land of Iraq to the land of Ash-Sham. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, that he said regarding this verse: We have blessed it for the worlds. He said: It is not fresh, pure water that descends to the rock in the Holy House. He said: Then it disperses in the earth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds, he said: To the Levant. Others said: Rather, it means Mecca, which is the land of which God Almighty said: Which We have blessed for the worlds. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds meaning Mecca, and Ishmael’s descent into the House. Do you not see that He says: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Makkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds (Al Imran 3:96). Abu Ja`far said: We chose what we chose from the statement on this matter because there is no disagreement among all the people of knowledge that Abraham’s migration from Iraq was to the Levant, and that he resided there during his life, even though he had come to Mecca and built the House there, and his son Ishmael settled him with Hagar’s slave girl. However, he did not reside there, and he did not make it a homeland for himself, nor did Lot. God only informed us about Abraham and Lot that He saved them to the land that He blessed for the worlds.
21:72: God Almighty says: And We gave to Abraham a son, and Jacob his son's son, as an extra gift to you. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His saying an extra gift. Some of them said: He meant Jacob specifically. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, meaning: And We gave him Isaac as a son, and Jacob as a son’s son as an additional gift. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift. The additional gift is the son of his grandson, Jacob. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, he said: He asked for one and said: My Lord, grant me from among the righteous, so He gave him one, and added to him Jacob, and Jacob was the son of his son. Others said: Rather, he meant Isaac and Jacob. They said: The meaning of the voluntary gift is the gift, and they are both from God’s gift that He gave them. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, he said: A gift. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Isaac and Jacob as a gift, he said: Ata’. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Abu Jaafar said: We have previously explained that a voluntary gift is the surplus of something that comes to a man, no matter what it is. Both of his sons, Isaac and Jacob, were a surplus from God that He bestowed upon Abraham, and a gift from Him to him. It is possible that he meant that he gave them both as a gift from him to him, and that they meant that he gave him Jacob’s gift, but there is no proof indicating which of the two is meant by the statement, so nothing is more appropriate to say about that than what God said, and God gave Abraham Isaac and Jacob as a gift. And His statement: And both of them We made righteous means working in obedience to God, avoiding what He has forbidden. And what He meant by His statement: Both of them is Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And His statement: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command means the Most High said: And We made Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob leaders to be followed in goodness, in obedience to God, in following His commands and prohibitions, and they were followed and they were followed in their actions. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command God made them leaders to be followed in the command of God. And his statement: guiding by Our command means: they guide the people by God’s command to them to do that, and they call them to God and to His worship. And his statement: And We inspired them to do good deeds means God Almighty says: And We inspired in what We inspired them to do good deeds, and establish prayer by Our command to do that. And they were worshippers of Us means: they were humble to Us, not arrogant about obeying and worshipping Us.
21:73: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired in them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakat, and they were worshippers of Us.
21:74: The Most High says: And We gave Lot wisdom, which is the settlement of disputes between opponents, and knowledge. He says: And We also gave him knowledge of the matter of his religion, and what is required of him for God of His obligations. There are two aspects to the accusative case of Lot: one is to accusative because the waw is attached to the verb, as we said: And We gave Lot, and the other is because of an implied word meaning: And remember Lot. And His statement: And We saved him from the town that was doing evil deeds means: And We saved him from Our punishment that We brought upon the people of the town that was doing evil deeds, and it was the town of Sodom to whose people Lot was sent, and the evil deeds that they were doing were: coming to men from behind, and throwing people at them, and farting in their gatherings, along with other evil things that they were doing, so God expelled him when He wanted to destroy them to Ash-Sham. As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: God brought them out, meaning Lot and his two daughters, Zayth and Za’artha, to the Levant when He wanted to destroy his people. His saying: Indeed, they were an evil and wicked people, disobeying God’s command, going against His obedience and the actions that He approves of.
21:75: God Almighty says: And We admitted Lot into Our mercy by saving him from the torment and affliction We inflicted upon his people, and by rescuing him from it. Indeed, he was among the righteous. He says: Indeed, Lot was among those who acted in obedience to Us, and desisted from Our commands and prohibitions and did not disobey Us. Ibn Zayd used to say about the meaning of his saying: And We admitted him into Our mercy what: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: And We admitted him into Our mercy, he said: Into Islam.
21:76: God the Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, Noah, when he called upon his Lord before you, and before Abraham and Lot, and asked Us to destroy his people who denied God in what He promised them of His threat, and denied Noah in what he brought them of the truth from his Lord, And Noah said, ‘My Lord, leave not upon the earth of the disbelievers a single dweller’ (Nuh 71:26). So We answered his call, and saved him and his family, meaning by his family: the people of faith from his children and their wives, from the great distress, meaning by the great Lord: the punishment that befell the deniers of the flood and drowning. Distress: intense grief, it is said: This matter has distressed me, so it distresses me greatly. And His statement: And We gave him victory over the people who denied Our signs, meaning: And We gave Noah victory over the people who denied Our proofs and evidence, so We saved him from them, and We drowned them all. Indeed, they were an evil people. God Almighty says: Indeed, the people of Noah who denied Our signs were an evil people, who did evil deeds, disobeyed God and went against His command.
21:77: "And We gave him victory over the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all."
21:78: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field. The people of interpretation differed about what that cultivation was. Some of them said: It was a plant. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, regarding his statement: When they gave judgment concerning the field, he said: The field was a plant. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that the sheep of the people fell into a field at night. Others said: Rather, that crop was a vineyard. Mention of those who said that: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement, And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, he said: A vineyard had produced its clusters. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Shureih, he said: Al-Harith was generous. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is what God Almighty said: When they gave judgment concerning the tillage. The tillage is the tillage of the land. We mean that it is possible that it was a crop, and it is possible that it was a planting, and it is not harmful to be ignorant of which of them it was. And His statement: When the sheep of the people pastured therein means: When the sheep of the other people, other than the people of the field, entered this field at night, pastured it or spoiled it. And We were witnesses to their judgment means: And We were witnesses to the judgment of David and Solomon and the people between whom they judged regarding what the sheep of the people of the sheep spoiled from the field of the people of the field, nothing of it was hidden from Us, and its knowledge was not hidden from Us. And His statement: So We made it clear means: So We made the case clear in that of Solomon without David, And to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge means: And all of them from David and Solomon and the messengers whom He mentioned at the beginning of this surah We gave judgment, which is prophethood, and knowledge: meaning and knowledge of the rulings of God. And what we said about that is inclined, said the people of interpretation. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, regarding his statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had pastured therein, he said: A vineyard had produced its clusters and spoiled it. He said: So David ruled that the sheep should go to the owner of the vineyard, but Solomon said: Other than that, O Prophet of God. He said: What is that? He said: The vineyard should be given to the owner of the sheep, so he takes care of it until it returns to how it was. The vineyard was given to its owner, and the sheep were given to their owner. That is what he said: So We made Solomon understand it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field... to His statement: And We were witnesses to their judgment, meaning: We were witnesses to their judgment. That was because two men entered upon David, one of them a farmer and the other a sheep owner. The farmer said: This man has let his sheep into my field, and nothing of my field remains. David said to him: Go, for all the sheep are yours. So David ruled accordingly. The sheep owner passed by Solomon and told him what David had ruled. So Solomon entered upon David and said: O Prophet of God, the judgment is different from what you have narrated. He said: How? Solomon said: The crop is not hidden from its owner what comes out of it every year, so he has the right from the owner of the sheep to sell their offspring, wool and hair until he gets the price of the crop, because the sheep have offspring every year. So David said: You have hit the mark, the judgment is as you have judged. So God made Solomon understand. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, he said: K narrated to me Khalifa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: David ruled that the sheep should go to the owners of the farm. Then the shepherds went out with their dogs, and Solomon said: How did he rule between you? So they told him, and he said: If I had been in your company, I would have ruled differently. So David was informed of that, so he called him and said: How will you rule between them? He said: I will give the sheep to the owners of the farm, so they will have their offspring, milk, offal, and benefits, and the owners of the sheep will sow for the owners of the farm the same as their crops. Then when the crops reach what they were on, the owners of the crops will take the crops and return the sheep to their owners. Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: When the sheep of the people pastured therein, he said: David gave them the necks of the sheep for cultivation, and Solomon ruled that the fleece and milk of the sheep belonged to the people of cultivation, and they were to tend them to the people of cultivation, and the people of the sheep would cultivate for them until the cultivation was as it was on the day it was eaten, then they would give it to its people, and they would take their sheep. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me something similar, except that he said: And they are responsible for herding it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Marra, regarding his statement: When the sheep of the people pastured therein, he said: The field was vegetation, and it was pastured therein at night, so they disputed about it before David, and he ruled that the sheep should go to the owners of the field. So they passed by Solomon and mentioned that to him, and he said: No, the sheep should be given away so that they may take some of them, meaning the owners of the field, and these people should take care of their field, and when it is returned to them, then the verse was revealed: So We made Solomon understand it. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Shuraih, regarding his statement: When the sheep of the people pastured therein, he said: The pasturing was at night, and the tillage was vineyard. So David gave the sheep to the owner of the vineyard. So Solomon said: The owner of the vineyard has the root of his land and the root of his vineyard left, so give him their wool and milk. He said: So this is the statement of God: So We gave Solomon understanding of it. Ibn Abi Ziyad told us: Yazid bin Harun told us: Ismail told us, on the authority of Aamer, who said: Two men came to Shuraih, and one of them said: This sheep of mine cut some of my yarn. Shuraih said: During the day or at night? He said: If it was during the day, then the owner of the sheep was absolved, and if it was at night, then he was liable. Then he recited: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had pastured therein. He said: The pasturing was at night. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Shureih, something similar. Yaqoub told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shuraih, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field... the verse, the plucking at night, and the shearing during the day. And it was mentioned to us that the sheep of the people fell into the crops at night, so that was brought to David, so he ruled that the sheep belonged to the owners of the crops, but Solomon said: It is not like that, but he has their offspring, their messengers, their shears, and their shears, until the next year is like the day of eating, the sheep are given to their owner, and the owner of the crop takes possession of his crop, so God said: And We made Solomon understand it. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Zuhri: When the sheep of the people were pastured therein. He said: The sheep were pastured in the field of a people. Al-Zuhri said: And pasturing only occurs at night, so David decided to take the sheep, and God made Solomon understand. He said: So when he was informed of David's decision, he said: No, but take the sheep, and you will have what comes out of their young and their young and their wool within a year. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: When the sheep of the people pastured therein, he said: So a people plowed. Muammar said: Al-Zuhri said: Plowing does not occur except at night, and plowing during the day. Qatada said: So He decreed that they should take the sheep, and God made Sulayman understand it, then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A’la. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had pastured therein... the two verses, he said: A man’s sheep got loose on another man’s field and ate it, so it came to David, and he ruled that the sheep belonged to the owner of the field because of what they had eaten, and it was as if he saw that this was the right way to do so, so they passed by Solomon, and he said: What has the Prophet of God ruled between you? So they told him, and he said: Shall I not rule between you, perhaps you will be satisfied with it? They said: Yes. He said: As for you, O owner of the farm, take this man’s sheep and be with them as their owner was, take from their milk and their udders and so on and so forth as he used to take, and you, O owner of the sheep, plow this man’s field until his plowing is like the one you did last night and your sheep pasture in it, then give him his field and take your sheep. This is the saying of God, the Blessed and Exalted: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field when the sheep of the people pastured therein. And he recited until he reached His saying: And to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: When the sheep of the people grazed therein, he said: They grazed. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Al-Nafsh: the flock at night. He said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Haram bin Muhaysa bin Mas`ud, who said: “A she-camel belonging to Al-Bara’ bin Azib entered the garden of some of the Ansar and damaged it. This was reported to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Because the sheep of the people were grazing in it.’ So he ruled against Al-Bara’ for what the she-camel had damaged, and he said: ‘It is upon the owners of livestock to guard the livestock at night, and it is upon the owners of gardens to guard their gardens during the day.’” Al-Zuhri said: The judgment of David and Solomon in this regard was that a man’s livestock entered a man’s field and spoiled it, and spoiling only occurs at night. So they went up to David, and he ruled that the sheep of the owner of the sheep belonged to the owner of the field. They returned and passed by Solomon, who said: How did the Prophet of God rule between you? They said: He ruled that the sheep belonged to the owner of the field. He said: The judgment is on this man’s caravan, return with me. So he came to his father David and said: O Prophet of God, you ruled that this man’s sheep belonged to the owner of the field. He said: Yes. He said: O Prophet of God, the judgment is on something other than this. He said: How so, my son? He said: The sheep are given to the owner of the crop, so he gets some of their milk, fat and wool, and the crop is given to the owner of the sheep to take care of it. When the crop returns to the condition in which the sheep had taken it, the sheep are returned to the owner of the sheep, and the crop is returned to the owner of the crop. David said: May God cut off your mouth, so he ruled as Solomon ruled. Al-Zuhri said: That is what he said: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field... to his saying: with judgment and knowledge.
