Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah and Ali ibn Mujahid told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone who heard al-Hasan say told me: The ruling was what Solomon decided, and God did not punish David in his ruling. And His statement: And We subjected to David the mountains and the birds, to glorify [God], God Almighty says: And We subjected to David the mountains and the birds, to glorify [God] when Ma’ad glorifies. Qatada used to say about the meaning of His statement: to glorify [God] in this place what: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We subjected to David the mountains, to glorify God, and the birds: meaning, they pray with David when he prays. And His saying: And We were to do it means: And We had decided that We would do that, and that We would subjugate the mountains and the birds in the Mother of the Book, with David, peace and blessings be upon him. 21:79: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “So We gave Solomon understanding of it, and to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected with David the mountains to glorify God, and the birds, and We were the Doers.”
21:80: God Almighty says: And We taught David the making of coats of mail for you. And among the Arabs, coats of mail are all weapons, whether they be armor, shields, swords, or spears. This is indicated by the words of Al-Hudhali: I have a robe for dressing, like a silk on the forehead of a frightened sheep. He is describing a spear with that. As for this place, the people of interpretation said: He meant armor. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you... the verse, he said: Before David, there were plates, he said: And the first to make these rings and chains was David. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you. He said: They were plates, and the first to string and shave them was David, peace be upon him. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: to protect you. Most of the reciters in the regions read it li-hasankum with a ya, meaning: to protect you from your violence. They mentioned it because the violence is masculine. Abu Ja’far Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’ read it li-hasankum with a ta, meaning: to protect you from the craft, so it was made feminine because the craft is feminine. Shaybah ibn Nasah and Asim ibn Abi al-Najud read li-hasankum with a nun, meaning: to protect you from your violence. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it with the letter ya`, because it is the reading that is the proof from the readers of the regions, even though the three readings that we mentioned are close in meaning, and that is because the craft is the clothing, and the clothing is the craft, and God is the one who is protected from violence, and He is the one who is protected by God making him thus, and the meaning of His statement: To protect you is to safeguard you, and they are from His statement: So-and-so has protected his slave girl. We have explained the meaning of that with its evidence in what came before. And violence is fighting, and We taught David the making of weapons for you to protect you when you wear them, and with them you meet your enemies from being killed. And His saying: Are you then grateful? He says: Are you, O people, grateful to God for His blessings upon you in what He taught you of the craft of making protective clothing for war and other blessings upon you? He says: So thank Me for that.
21:81: God Almighty says: And We subjected to Solomon, son of David, the wind, a violent storm. Its violent force is its strong blowing. It ran by his command to the land which We had blessed. He says: The wind ran by Solomon’s command to the land which We had blessed, meaning: to the Levant. This is because it ran with Solomon and his companions to wherever Solomon wanted, then returned with him to his home in the Levant. That is why it was said: to the land which We had blessed. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When Solomon went out to his council, the birds would flock to him, and the jinn and humans would stand up for him until he sat on his throne. He was a man of war, who rarely sat down from war, and he would not hear of a king in any part of the earth except that he would come to him and humiliate him. And it was claimed that when he wanted to wage war, he would order his army to be set up and a piece of wood would be pitched for him, then he would set up a place for him on the wood, then he would load the people and the beasts and all the war equipment on it, until when he had carried what he wanted, he would order the wind to blow with him, so it would enter under that wood and carry him, until it had become independent of the wind, so it would extend his journey for a month, and his journey for a month in the morning to wherever he wanted. God Almighty says: So We subjected to him the wind, blowing gently at his command wherever he desired (Sad: 36). He said: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, its morning journey was a month and its evening journey was a month (Saba 34:12). He said: He mentioned to me that we found a house and a building in the area. We went from Istakhr and said, We will leave from it, God willing, and we will say, ‘Sham.’ Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, which was strong... to his statement: And We were their guardians. He said: God made Solomon inherit David, so He made him inherit his prophethood and his kingdom, and He increased that by making the wind and the devils subservient to him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, blowing by his command, he said: A violent wind blowing by his command to the land which We have blessed, he said: Ash-Sham. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: And to Solomon was the wind. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it in the accusative case, based on the meaning we mentioned. Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj read the wind in the nominative case, with the subject in Solomon, as the beginning of the report that Solomon was the wind. Abu Jaafar said: The reading that I do not permit reading other than it in this regard is what the readers of the regions have agreed upon, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it. And His statement: And We were Knowing of all things means: And We were Knowing of what We did for Solomon in terms of subjecting him to Him, and giving him what We gave him of the kingdom and the goodness of creation, so We acted based on Our knowledge of the place of what We did to him of that, and We are Knowing of all things, nothing of it is hidden from Us.
21:82: God Almighty says: And We also subjected to Solomon some of the devils who would dive for him in the sea, and they would teach him work other than that, such as building, statues, and shrines. And We were their guardians. He says, “And We were their guardians of their deeds and their numbers. It does not burden Us to preserve all of that.”
21:83: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember Job, O Muhammad, when he called upon his Lord, and distress and affliction had befallen him, My Lord, indeed distress has befallen me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. So We answered him. God Almighty says: So We answered Job’s prayer when he called upon Us, and We removed the distress, affliction, and hardship that he had been suffering from. The distress that befell him and the affliction that descended upon him were a test and trial from God for him. The reason for this was as follows: Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar Al-Bukhari told me: Ismail bin Ubaj Al-Karim bin Hisham told us: Abd Al-Samad bin Muqal told us: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: The beginning of the matter of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God’s prayers be upon him, was that he was patient and a good servant. Wahb said: Gabriel has a position before God that no other angel has in terms of closeness to God and virtue with Him. Gabriel is the one who receives speech. If a servant of God is mentioned in a good way, Gabriel receives him from him, then Michael receives him, and the angels who are close to God surround the Throne. This spreads among the angels who are close to God, and the prayer for that servant became from the people of the heavens. If the angels of the heavens pray for him, they descend upon him with the prayer to the angels of the earth. Satan was not veiled by anything in the heavens, and he would stand in them wherever he wanted as they wanted. From there, he reached Adam when he expelled him from Paradise. He continued to ascend in the heavens until God sent Jesus, son of Mary. He was veiled from four, and he used to ascend in three. When God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was veiled from the remaining three. He and all of his soldiers are veiled from all the heavens until the Day of Resurrection, Except for one who steals a hearing and is pursued by a bright flame. (al-Hijr 15:15) 18) Therefore, the jinn denied what they knew until the day they said: And we sought the heaven but found it filled with stern guards (al-Jinn 72:8)… until His saying: A meteor lying in wait (al-Jinn 72:9). Wahb said: Iblis was not alarmed except by the response of the angels by praying for Job, and that was when God mentioned him and praised him. When Iblis heard the prayer of the angels, he was overcome by envy and malice, and he quickly ascended until he stopped in front of God in a place where he used to stop. He said: O my God, I looked into the matter of your servant Abu Bakr, and I found him to be a servant upon whom you bestowed blessings and he thanked you, and you granted him well-being and he praised you, then you did not test him with severity and you did not test him with a trial, and I am your guarantor: if you strike him with a trial, he will disbelieve in you and forget you, and worship other than you. God the Blessed and Exalted said to him: Go, for I have given you authority over his wealth, for it is the matter for which you claim that he thanks Me. You have no authority over his body or mind. So the enemy of God pounced until he fell to the ground. Then he gathered the demons of the devils and their leaders. Job had all of Bathniyah in Syria, including its east and west. He had a thousand sheep with their shepherds, and five hundred acres, followed by five hundred slaves, each slave had a wife, children, and wealth. Each acre carried a donkey that gave birth to two, three, four, five, and more than that. When Iblis gathered the devils, he said to them: What power and knowledge do you have? I have been given authority over Job’s wealth, for it is a great calamity and a trial that men cannot bear. An evil demon from the devils said: I have been given such power that if I wish I can turn into a hurricane of fire, burning everything I come across. Iblis said to him: Go to the camels and their shepherds. So he went and led the camels, and that was when they laid their heads down and were fixed in Its pastures, and people did not notice until a hurricane of fire rose from under the ground, from which the spirits of poisons blew, and no one approached it except that he was burned. He continued to burn it and its shepherds until he reached the end of it. When he finished, Satan appeared on a seated camel with its shepherd. Then he set out to lead Job until he found him standing praying. He said: O Job! He said: At your service. He said: Do you know what your Lord, whom you chose, worshipped and declared to be One, did with your camels and their shepherds? Job said: They are His property that we have lent them, and He is more deserving of them if He wishes to take them away. I have long since prepared myself and my property to perish. Satan said: Your Lord sent upon it a fire from the sky, and it burned up its shepherds, until it destroyed every last thing of it and its shepherds. It left the people astounded, as they stood there amazed. Some of them said: Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion. Some of them said: If Job’s God had the power to prevent any of that, He would have prevented it for him. Some of them said: Rather, he did what he did, so that his enemy might gloat over it and his friend might be saddened by it. Job said: Praise be to God when He gave me and when He took from me. Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked I shall return to the dust, and naked I shall be gathered to God. It is not appropriate for you to rejoice when God lends you and to grieve when He takes away His loan. God is more deserving of you and of what He has given you. If God had known any good in you, O servant, He would have transferred your soul with the King of Spirits, so He would have rewarded me for you, and you would have become a witness. But He has done evil to you, so He delayed you because of it. So God saved you from the calamity and saved you from the affliction, just as the tares are saved from the wheat. Then Iblis returned to his companions, humiliated and disgraced, and said to them: What power do you have? For I did not speak to his heart. An Ifrit from their leaders said: I have such power that if I wish, I can make a sound that no living being hears without his soul coming out. Iblis said to him: Go to the sheep and their shepherds. So he set out leading the sheep and their shepherds, until he reached the middle of them and cried out a sound that made them all crouch dead, along with their shepherds. Then Iblis came out in disguise, defeating the shepherds, until he came to Job and found him standing praying. He said to him the first thing, and Job gave him the same answer. Then Iblis returned to his companions and said to them: What power do you have? For I did not speak to Job’s heart. An Ifrit from their leaders said: I have such power that if I wish, I can turn into a violent wind that blows away everything it comes upon, until I leave nothing behind. Iblis said to him: Go to the fields and the crops. So he set out leading them. And when they had brought the acres near, and had set up in the field, and the donkeys and their young were pasturing, they did not notice until a violent wind blew, and blew away everything from that, until it was as if it had never been. Then Satan came out in the form of a farmer, until he came to Job while he was standing praying, and he said to him the same as he had said before, and Job responded to him the same as he had responded before. When Satan saw that he had spent his money and had not succeeded in it, he quickly ascended until he stood before God in the same position he had been standing before: O my God, Job sees that you did not give him enjoyment of himself and his son, so you gave him money, so will you give me power over his son? It is the misleading trial, and the calamity that men’s hearts cannot stand, and their patience cannot bear. So God Almighty said to him: Go, for I have given you authority over his son, and you have no authority over his heart, nor his body, nor his mind. So the enemy of God pounced on his horse, until he came to the sons of Ayyub while they were in their palace, and he continued to shake them until it collapsed from its foundations. Then he began to butt the walls against each other, and to throw wood and stones at them, until when he had mutilated them all, he raised the palace with it, until when he had lowered it with them, they were in it, lying face down. Ayyub set out, imitating the teacher who taught them wisdom, and he was wounded, his face torn, his blood flowing, and his brain changed, and he could hardly recognize him from the severity of the change and the mutilation in which he came. When Ayyub looked at him, he was terrified, and he was sad, and his eyes teared up, and he said to him: O Ayyub, if you had seen how he escaped from where he escaped, and what he threw at us from above us and from below us, and if you had seen between you how they were tortured, and how they were mutilated, and how they were turned upside down, so they were… They were lying on their heads, their blood and brains flowing from their noses and cavities, and dripping from their eyelashes. If you had seen how their bellies were split open, and their intestines scattered, and if you had seen how they were thrown with wood and stones, their brains being smashed, and how the wood crushed their bones, pierced their skin, and severed their nerves, and if you had seen the nerves exposed, and if you had seen the bones shattered in the cavities, and if you had seen the faces smashed, and if you had seen the walls butting up against them, and if you had seen what you saw, your heart would have been cut off. He kept saying this and similar things, and he kept softening him until Job softened and cried, and took a handful of dirt and placed it on his head. Satan seized the opportunity from him at that time, and he quickly ascended, who had been from Job’s grief, pleased with him. Then Job did not take long to recover and see, so he sought forgiveness, and his companions from the angels ascended with his repentance, so Satan hastened to God, and found that he had known of what had been raised to him from Job’s repentance. Then Satan stood, humiliated and disgraced, and said: O my God, the only thing that has made the danger of wealth and children easy for Job is that he sees that you did not give him pleasure in himself, so you will return the wealth and children to him. Do you have power over his body? Then I am your guarantor that if you test him in his body, he will forget you, deny you, and deny your favor. God said: Go, I have given you power over his body, but you have no power over his tongue, nor over his heart, nor over his mind. Then the enemy of God pounced on his horse and found Job prostrating. He hurried before he could raise his head, and came to him from the ground in the place of his face. He blew into his nostrils, and his body was set on fire, and he became flabby, and warts grew on him like the buttocks of sheep, and he suffered from an itch that he could not control. He scratched with his nails until they all fell off, then he scratched with bones, and he scratched with rough stones, and with pieces of rough sackcloth, scratching until his flesh was used up and torn. When Job’s skin became swollen and changed and stinking, the people of the village took him out, and they put him on a hill, and they made two huts for him, and God’s creation rejected him except his wife, who would go to him with what would fix him and make him stick. Three of his companions followed him in his religion, but when they saw what God had afflicted him with, they rejected him, without abandoning his religion, and they accused him. One of them was called Baldad, Alifez, and Safir. He said: So the three went to him while he was in his affliction. So they wept for him, and when he heard them, he turned to his Lord and said: “My Lord, for what did You create me? And if You had abandoned me when I was in a state of dislike, You would have left me and not created me. I wish I had been a menstrual period that my mother threw up, and I wish I had died in her womb, so that I would not have known anything and she would not have known me. What sin have I committed that no one else has committed? And what deed have I done that You have turned Your noble face away from me?” If you had killed me and joined me to my fathers, death would have been more beautiful for me. So, as an example for me are the sultans who were lined up before them, striking them with swords, out of stinginess with death, and keen on their survival, they became kneeling in their graves, until they thought they would live forever. And as an example for me are the kings who hoarded treasures, buried dungeons, and gathered crowds, and thought they would live forever. And as an example for me are the tyrants who built cities and fortresses, and lived in them for hundreds of years, then they became ruins, a refuge for beasts, and a refuge for devils. Alifiz At-Taymani said: We are exhausted by your matter, O Ayoub. If we speak to you, we do not expect to talk from you, and if we remain silent about you despite the affliction we see in you, that is against us. We saw from your deeds deeds for which we expected from you a reward other than what we saw. A man reaps what he sows and is rewarded for what he has done. I bear witness to God, whose greatness cannot be measured, and whose blessings cannot be counted. He who sends down water from the sky, thereby giving life to the dead, raising up what is low, and strengthening the weak. He whose wisdom causes the wise to go astray before His wisdom, and the knowledge of the learned before His knowledge, until you see them floundering in darkness. He who hopes for God’s help is the strong one, and he who relies on Him is the one who is sufficient. He is the one who breaks and mends, and wounds and heals. Job said: Therefore I kept silent, bit my tongue, and lowered my head for bad service, because I knew that his punishment had changed the light of my face, and that his power had taken away the strength of my body. I am his servant, whatever he decreed for me has befallen me, and I have no strength except what he has carried on me. If my bones were iron, and my body of brass, and my heart of stone, I could not bear this matter, but he has tested me, and he is carrying it for me. You came to me angry, you were terrified before you were terrified, and you wept before you were struck. How would I be if I said to you: Give charity on my behalf from your money, perhaps God will save me, or offer an offering on my behalf, perhaps God will accept it from me and be pleased with me? When I wake up, I wish to sleep, hoping to rest, but when I sleep, my soul almost dies. My fingers are cut off, so I lift a morsel of food with both hands, but they do not reach my mouth except with effort from me. My uvula has fallen out, and my head is hollow, so there is no blockage between my ears, so that one of them can be seen from the other, and my brain is dripping from my mouth. My hair has fallen out of me, as if my face had been burned by fire, and my pupils are hanging down over my cheeks. My tongue has swelled until it has filled my mouth, so I cannot put food in it without it sticking out. My lips have swelled until the upper part covers my nose and the lower part covers my chin. My intestines have been cut off in my stomach, so I put food in and it comes out as it went in, I do not feel it and it does not benefit me. The strength of my legs has gone, so they are as if they are filled water skins, and I cannot carry them. I carry my blanket with my hands and teeth, but I cannot carry it until someone else carries it with me. The money has gone, so I have begun to beg with my palm. And the one I was supporting would feed me a single morsel, and he would favor me with it and reproach me. My sons and daughters have perished, and if any of them had remained, they would have helped me in my affliction and benefited me. And the torment is not like the torment of this world. It is removed from its people and they die from it, but blessed is he who has comfort in the home whose people do not die, and they do not move from their homes. Happy is he who is happy there, and wretched is he who is wretched in it. Bildad said: How can your tongue bear this saying, and how can you utter it? Do you say that the just are unjust, or do you say that the strong are weak? Weep over your sin, and implore your Lord; perhaps He will have mercy on you and forgive your fault, and perhaps, if you are innocent, He will make this a provision for you in the hereafter. But if your heart has hardened, then our saying will not benefit you, and it will not take away how he hopes to prevent it. How can he who denies the truth hope to fulfill his right? Ayyub said: I know that this is the truth. The servant will not succeed against his Lord, nor will he be able to argue with Him. So what can I say to Him, if I have the power? He is the One who raised the heaven and established it alone. He is the One who scrapes it when He wills, so it folds up for Him. He is the One who flattened the earth and spread it out alone, and erected the firm mountains therein. Then it is He who shakes it from its roots until its lowest parts become its highest parts. And if it is about speech, what can I say to Him? He who created the Mighty Throne with a single word, and filled it with the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them of creation, and expanded it while it is in a vast expanse. He is the One who spoke to the seas so they understood His words, and He commanded them so they did not return to His command. He is the One who makes the whales and the birds and every creature understand. He is the One who speaks to the dead so He brings them back to life with His words. He speaks to the stones so they understand His words, and He commands them so they obey Him. Alifez said: What you say is great, O Job. The skins shudder at the mention of what you say. What happened to you happened to you without any sin you committed. Such severity and this speech brought you down to this position. Your sin was great, and your demands were many. You usurped the wealth of the wealthy. You dressed while they were naked, and ate while they were hungry. You locked your door from the weak, and your food from the hungry, and your kindness from the needy. You kept that secret and hid it in your house. You displayed deeds that we saw you doing. So you thought that God would not reward you for what appeared from you. You thought that God does not know what you concealed in your house. How could He not know that when He knows what the earths conceal, and what is under the darkness and the air? Job, peace be upon him, said: If I speak, speech will not benefit me, and if I remain silent, you will not excuse me. My plot has befallen me, and I have angered my Lord with my sin, and let my enemies rejoice, and have given them power over me, and made me a target for affliction, and made me a target for temptation. You did not relieve me despite that, but rather followed me with one affliction after another. Was I not a home for the stranger, and a place of rest for the poor, and a guardian for the orphan, and a guardian for the widow? I have not seen a stranger except that I was a home for him in place of his home, and a place of rest in place of his rest. I have not seen a mother except that I was a guardian for her, pleased with his upkeep, and I am a humble slave. If I do good, I have no words to say good, because the favor is for my Lord and not for me, and if I do evil, then in His hand is my punishment. And a affliction has befallen me, if I were to set it on a mountain that would be too weak to bear it, how could my weakness bear it? Eliphaz said: Do you argue with God, Job, about His affair? Or do you want to be fair to Him, though you are a sinner, or acquit her, though you are not? He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and has counted what is in them of creation, so how could He not know what you concealed, and how could He not know what you did, and reward you for it? God placed angels in rows around His throne, and in the corners of His heavens, then He concealed Himself with light, so His sight is dim from Him, and their strength is weak from Him, and their Mighty One is lowly before Him, and you claim that if He were to argue with you and come to judgment with you, would you see Him, so that you would be fair to Him? Or would you hear Him, so that you would converse with Him? We have known His judgment of you, for he who desires to be elevated, He will lower him, and he who humbles himself before Him, He will raise him. Job, peace be upon him, said: If He destroys me, who is there who will confront Him regarding His servant and ask Him about his affair? Nothing repels His wrath except His mercy, and nothing benefits His servant except supplication to Him. He said: O Lord, turn to me with Your mercy, and inform me of my sin that I have committed, or for what reason You have turned Your noble face away from me, and made me like an enemy to You, while You used to honor me? Nothing escapes You. You count the raindrops, the leaves of the trees, and the dust particles. My skin has become like a rotten garment. Whatever I hold, it falls into my hand. So grant me a sacrifice from You and relief from my affliction, with the power that resurrects the dead of the servants and disperses the dead of the lands. Do not destroy me without informing me of my sin, and do not spoil the work of Your hands, even though You are independent of me. There should be no injustice in Your judgment, nor any haste in Your vengeance. Only the weak need injustice, and only he who fears missing out hastens. Do not remind me of my mistakes and my sins. Remember how You created me from clay, then made me a lump of flesh, then created the lump of flesh into bones, and clothed the bones with flesh and skin, and made the nerves and veins for that purpose strength and strength. You raised me when I was small, and provided for me when I was old, then kept Your covenant and did Your command. If I erred, then explain to me, and do not destroy me with grief and inform me. My sin, if I do not please You, then I am worthy of Your punishment, and if I am among Your creation, You count my deeds, and I seek Your forgiveness, yet do not forgive me. If I do good, I do not raise my head, and if I do evil, You do not swallow my saliva, nor do You lift my stumble. You see my weakness beneath You, and my supplication to You. So why did You create me? Did You not bring me forth from my mother’s womb? If I were as one who did not exist, it would have been better for me. The world is not in danger of Your wrath, and my body is not able to bear Your punishment. So have mercy on me and let me taste the flavor of wellness, before I reach the narrowness of the grave, the darkness of the earth, and the grief of death. Safir said: You have spoken, O Ayoub, and no one can hold your mouth shut. You claim that you are innocent, but will it benefit you if you are innocent, and there is someone who counts your deeds? And you claim that you know that God will forgive you your sins. Do you know the height of the sky and how far it is? Or do you know the depth of the air and how far it is? Or do you know which land is the widest? Or do you have a measure for it by which you can estimate it? Or do you know which sea is the deepest? Or do you know how you can draw it? If you know this knowledge and if you do not know it, then God created it and He is counting it. If you stop talking a lot and ask your Lord, you hope that He will have mercy on you, and by that you will extract His mercy. If you persist in your sin and raise your hands to God when in need, and you insist on your sin like running water that cannot be held back, then when you ask the Most Merciful for needs, the faces of the wicked will darken and their eyes will darken, and then He will be pleased with the success of their needs, those who left desires to adorn themselves with that before their Lord, and advanced in supplication, so that they would deserve mercy when they needed it, and they are the ones who struggled at night, and isolated themselves from the beds, and waited for the trees. Job said: You are a people who have become arrogant towards yourselves. In the past, men used to respect me, but my right is known, I am fair to my opponents, I am the conqueror of those who conquer me today. He asks me about the knowledge of the unseen of God that I do not know, and he asks me. By my life, a brother does not advise his brother when a calamity befalls him like this, but he cries with him. If you are serious, then my mind falls short of what you are asking me about. So ask the birds of the sky, will they tell you? And ask the beasts of the earth, will they return to you? And ask the wild beasts, will they answer you? And ask the whales of the sea, will they describe to you all that you have counted? Know that He created this with His wisdom and prepared it with His kindness. Does not the son of Adam know of speech what he has heard with his ears, what he has tasted with his mouth, and what he has smelled with his nose? And that the knowledge you asked about is known only to God who created him? To Him belongs wisdom and might, and to Him belongs greatness and kindness, and to Him belongs majesty and power. If he corrupts, who is there to reform? And if he is mute, who is there to articulate? If we look at the seas, they dry up from fear of Him, and if He permits them, they swallow the earth. He is the One who carries them with His power. He is the One before whose kingdom kings are astounded, and before whose knowledge scholars are stunned. Before whose wisdom the wise are weary, and before whose power the falsifiers are humiliated. He is the One who remembers the forgotten, and forgets the remembered, and He causes darkness and light to flow. This is my knowledge, and His creation is greater than my mind can count, and His greatness is greater than someone like me can appreciate. Bildad said: The hypocrite will be rewarded for his secret hypocrisy, and the public deception he made will lead him astray, and he will be relied upon for the recompense he did, and his memory will perish in this world, and his light will be darkened in the Hereafter, and his path will be made desolate, and his inner self will ensnare him, and his name will be cut off from the earth, so there will be no mention of him or any development in it, and no righteous children will inherit him after him, and no origin will remain for him by which he can be known, and whoever sees him will be astonished, and poems will stop at his mention. Job said: If I am lost, then my loss is upon me. If I am innocent, then what protection do I have? If I cry out, who will help me cry out? If I keep silent, who will excuse me? My hope is gone, my dreams are shattered, and my acquaintances have rejected me. I called my servant, but he did not answer me. I implored my maidservant, but she did not have mercy on me. Calamity befell me, but they rejected me. You were more severe upon me than my calamity. Look and be amazed at the wonders in my body. Have you not heard what has befallen me? And what has been your preoccupation with me? If a servant were to dispute with his Lord, I would hope to prevail in judgment. But I have a Lord, Omnipotent, Exalted above His heavens, and He has thrown me here, and I am insignificant to Him. They do not excuse me with my excuse, nor do they bring me near. So I plead for myself. He hears me and I do not hear Him, He sees me and I do not see Him, and He encompasses me. If He were to appear to me, my kidneys would melt, my soul would be stunned, and if He were to breathe, I would speak at the top of my lungs, and He would strip me of all awe. I would know for what sin He has tormented me. It was called out, O Job! He said, At your service! He said, "I am this one who has come near to you. Rise, tighten your belt, and take the place of a tyrant. It is not fitting for anyone to contend with me except a tyrant like me, and it is not fitting for anyone to contend with me except one who puts the reins in the mouth of a lion, the young lambs in the mouth of a phoenix, and the meat in the mouth of a dragon, who measures a measure of light, weighs a mithqal of wind, and binds a bundle of the sun, who returns yesterday to tomorrow. Your soul has granted you a matter that cannot be achieved with your strength. If, when your soul granted you that and called you to it, you had remembered what aim it sought for you, did you want to contend with me out of your oppression, or did you want to argue with me about your mistake, or did you want to outdo me with your weakness? Where were you in relation to me on the day I created the earth and placed it on its foundation? Did you know the extent of its power? Or were you with me, passing through its edges? Or do you know what is beyond its corners? Or on what were you placed its edges? Was the water carrying the earth with your obedience? Or was the earth, by your wisdom, a covering for the water? Where were you from me on the day You raised the sky as a ceiling in the air, with no ties fixed above it, nor supported by pillars beneath it? Is your wisdom sufficient to cause its light to flow, or its stars to move, or its night and day to differ by your command? Where were you from me on the day You filled the seas and caused the rivers to spring forth? Did your power hold back the waves of the seas at their limits, or did your power open the wombs when they reached their term? Where were you from me on the day You poured water on the earth and erected the lofty mountains? Did you have an arm that could bear it? Or do you know how many mithqals are in them? Or where is the water that was sent down from the sky? Do you know what a mother gives birth to? Did your wisdom count the rain and divide the provisions, or does your power stir up the clouds and cover them with water? Do you know what the sounds of thunder are? Or from what does the lightning flash? Have you seen the depth of the seas? Or do you know what is beyond the air? Or have you stored the souls of the dead? Or do you know where the storehouse of snow is, or where the storehouses of hail are? Or where are the mountains of hail? Or do you know where the night's treasury is in the day, and where the day's treasury is in the night, and where is the path of light? And in what language do trees speak? And where is the wind's treasury, and how do the locks hold it? And who made the minds in the hearts of men? And who split the ears and the eyes, and from that the angels for His kingdom? And who subdued the tyrants with His might? And divided the provisions of the beasts with His wisdom? And who divided the provisions of the lion? And made the bird know its livelihoods, and made it kind to its chicks? Who freed the beasts from service? And made its dwellings the wild? It does not tame sounds, nor does it fear the rulers? Is it from Your wisdom that the chicks of the birds branched out and became children for their mothers? Is it from Your wisdom that their mothers were kind to them, until they brought forth food for it from their bellies, and preferred living to their souls? Is it from Your wisdom that the eagle sees, and becomes in the places of the slain? Where were you from me when I created Bahamut? Its place is in the middle of the earth, and the two veins carry the mountains, the villages, and the cities. Their ears are like tall pine trees, their heads are like mountain peaks, the veins of their thighs are like iron pegs, their skins are like split rocks, and their bones are like pillars of copper. They are the heads of my creation whom I created for fighting. Did you fill their skins with flesh? Or did you fill their heads with brains? Or do you have a share in their creation? Or do you have the power that two hands created? Or does your power reach the point that you can crush their noses, or place your hand on their heads, or sit for them on a path and detain them, or prevent them from their food? Where were you when I created the dragon, and his sustenance was in the sea, and his dwelling was in the clouds? His eyes glowed with fire, and his nostrils burst with smoke. His lower part was like a bow of clouds, from which burst a flame like a hurricane of dust. His belly burned, and his soul was inflamed, and his foam was like rocks, and the gnashing of his teeth was like the sound of thunderbolts, and the sight of his eyes was like the flame of lightning. Worries do not enter his secrets. Armies pass by him while he reclines, and nothing frightens him that has no joint. Iron bars are like straw to him, and copper is like threads to him. He is not frightened by arrows, and does not feel the sound of rocks on his body, and he laughs at meteors, and he walks in the air like a bird, and destroys everything that passes by. The king of beasts, and it is him I have chosen with strength over my creation. Will you take him with your rope and tie him with his tongue? Or will you put the bridle in his jaw? Do you think he will fulfill your covenant? Or will he swim in fear of you? Do you count his lifespan? Or do you know his appointed time? Or if you will miss his sustenance? Or do you know what he has destroyed on earth? Or what he will destroy in the rest of his life? Can you bear his anger when he is angry? Or do you command him and he obeys you? Blessed be God the Most High. Ayyub (peace be upon him) said: I have fallen short of this matter that has befallen me. I wish the earth had split open with me, so that I could go about my affliction, and I would not have said anything that would anger my Lord. The affliction has gathered upon me. My God, You have made me like an enemy to You, and You have honored me and known my advice. You know that what I have mentioned is the work of Your hands and the planning of Your wisdom. And greater than this, You have done whatever You will. Nothing is beyond Your power, and nothing is hidden from You, and nothing is absent from You. Who is this who thinks that if You will, You can do it? Nothing is beyond Your power, and nothing is hidden from You, and nothing is absent from You. Who is this who thinks that a secret can be kept from You, and You know what crosses hearts? And I have learned from You in this affliction of mine what I did not know. And I feared when I tested Your matter more than I feared. I used to hear Your wrath by hearing, but now it is the sight of the eye. I spoke when You spoke so that You might excuse me, and I was silent when I was silent so that You might have mercy on me. A word that slipped, so I will not return. I have put my hand down. On my mouth, and I bit my tongue, and stuck my cheek to the dust, and buried my face in my children, and I was silent as my sin silenced me, so forgive me for what I said, for I will not return to anything you hate from me. God Almighty said: O Job, My knowledge has been fulfilled in you, and with My patience I have turned away My wrath from you. For you have sinned, I have forgiven you, and I have restored to you your family and your wealth and the like thereof with them. So wash yourself with this water, for in it is your healing, and make a sacrifice on behalf of your companions, and ask forgiveness for them, for they have disobeyed Me in you.
21:84: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So We responded to him and removed the affliction that was upon him, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani and others from the people of the first book, that it was from the hadith of Ayoub that he was a Roman man, and God had chosen him and given him knowledge, and tested him with wealth through many children and money, and had expanded the worldly life for him, and had made his provisions abundant for him. He had the upper and lower parts of the land of Ash-Sham, and he had in it all kinds of wealth, from camels, cows, sheep, horses and donkeys, such that no man would have a better number or number than him. God had given him a family and children, both men and women. He was pious, God-fearing, and merciful to the poor, feeding the poor, supporting widows, taking care of orphans, honoring the guest, and delivering to the wayfarer. He was grateful for God’s blessings upon him, fulfilling God’s right to wealth. He had refrained from God’s enemy, Satan, from afflicting him with what afflicts the rich of arrogance, heedlessness, and forgetfulness. And he was preoccupied with what he had of this world, and he was with three people who believed in him and confirmed him, and they knew the superiority of what God had given him over others, among them a man from Yemen called: Alifiz, and two men from his country, one of them called: Sofar and the other: Baldad, and they were old men from his country, and Iblis, the enemy of God, had a house in the seventh heaven where he would stay every year and be asked, so he ascended to heaven on the day in which he used to ascend, and God said to him, or it was said to him on behalf of God: Have you been able to do anything to My servant Job? He said: O Lord, how can I be able to do anything to him? Or you have tested him with ease, grace, abundance and well-being, and you have given him family, wealth, children, wealth and well-being in his body, family and wealth, so why should he not thank you, worship you and obey you, when you have done that to him? If you had tested him by taking away what you have given him, he would have changed from his thanking you and abandoning your worship, and he would have left your obedience to something else, or as the enemy of God said, so he said: I have given you power over his family and wealth, and God is the most knowing of him, and He did not give him power over him except as a mercy to increase his reward for the affliction that befalls him, and to make it a lesson for the patient, and a reminder for the worshippers in every affliction that befalls them, so that they may despair of him, and hope from the consequence of patience in the worldly life the reward of the Hereafter and what God did to Job, so the enemy of God descended quickly, so he gathered the demons of the jinn and the rebellious devils from his soldiers, and he said: I have given power over Job’s family and wealth, so what is upon you? Then one of them said: I will be a hurricane in which there is fire, and I will not pass by anything of his wealth except that I destroy it. He said: You can do that. So he went out until he came to his camels, and he burned them and their shepherds all together. Then the enemy of God came to Job in the form of his guardian over them while he was in a prayer place and said: O Job, a fire came until it covered your camels and burned them and everyone in them except me, so I came to you to inform you of that. Job recognized him and said: Praise be to God who gave it and took it, who brought you out of it as the tares are brought out of the pure grain. Then he turned away from him and began to gain money one by one until he reached the end of it. Whenever he reached the point of losing money from his wealth, he praised God and praised Him well and was satisfied with the decree, and prepared himself to be patient with the affliction, until when he had no money left, he came to his family and children, and they were in a palace with their attendants and servants. He appeared as a violent wind, and carried the palace from its sides and threw it on his family and children, crushing them beneath it. Then he came to him in the form of His commander over them, who had slapped his face, said: O Job, a violent wind has come, and has carried the palace from its sides, then thrown it upon your family and children, and has slapped them apart, so I have come to you to tell you about that. So he did not grieve over anything that had happened to him as he grieved over his family and children. He took some dirt and placed it on his head, then said: I wish my mother had not given birth to me, and that I was nothing. The enemy of God was pleased with her, so he ascended to heaven in joy. Job returned to repentance for what he had said, so he praised God, and his repentance preceded the enemy of God to God, and his return to him. He said: O Lord, give me power over his body. He said: I have given you power over his body except for his tongue, his heart, his soul, his hearing and his sight. So the enemy of God came to him while he was prostrating, and he blew into his body a breath that ignited what was between his horn and his feet, like the burning of fire. Then warts appeared on his body like the buttocks of sheep. He scratched with his nails until they were gone, then with pottery and stones until his flesh fell off, and nothing remained of him except the veins, nerves and bones. His eyes roamed in his head to see, and his heart was for reason, and he did not reach any of the stuffing of his stomach, because the soul cannot survive except through it. So he ate and drank in a twisted manner from his stuffing, and he remained like that as long as God willed him to remain. Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, he said: Wahb ibn Munabbih used to say: He remained in that affliction for three years, not exceeding one day, and when Job overcame him and could not do anything to him, he came to his wife in a form that was not like the form of the sons of Adam in size, body and height, on a mount that was not like the mounts of people, it had size, splendor and beauty that she did not have, and he said to her: Are you the companion of Job, this afflicted man? She said: Yes. He said: Do you know me? She said: No. He said: I am the god of the earth, and I am the one who did to your companion what I did, and that is because he worshipped the god of the heavens and left me, so he angered me, and if he prostrated to me once, I would return to him and to you all that you had of wealth and children, for they are with me. Then he showed them to her, as you can see, in the valley in which he met her. He said: I heard that he only said: If your companion ate food and did not say the name of God over it, he would be cured of his affliction, and God knows best. And the enemy of God wanted to come to him from her side, so she returned to Job and told him what he had said to her and what she had seen. He said: Has the enemy of God come to you to tempt you away from your religion? Then he swore that if God healed him, he would strike her a hundred times. When the affliction had become too long for him, those men who had been with him came to him and believed in him, with them a young man who had believed in him and believed in him. They sat with Job and looked at the affliction that had befallen him, and they were greatly amazed and horrified by it. Job, may God's prayers be upon him, was exhausted, and that was when God wanted to relieve him of what was afflicting him. When Job saw how great they were at what had befallen him, he said: O Lord, for what reason did You create me? And if when You had decreed the affliction You had left me and not created me, I would that I were blood that my mother had cast out. Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Ibn Askar, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Karim, to: And they endured the night, and kept away from the bed, and waited for the pre-dawn hours. Then he added to it: Those are the secure ones who do not fear, and do not worry, and do not grieve. So where is the outcome of your matter, O Job, compared to their consequences. A young man said, “He was present and heard what they said, but they did not pay attention to him and did not pay attention to his council. God’s decree for them was because of their injustice in speech and their excess. God wanted to make them look small to him and to belittle their dreams by making him small to them. When he spoke, he continued speaking, but he only increased in wisdom. It was the custom of the people to listen and be humble when they were admonished or reminded. So he said, ‘You spoke before me, O elders, and you were more deserving of speaking and more worthy of it than I am, because of your advanced age and because you experienced before me, and saw and knew what I did not know, and you knew what I did not know. Despite that, you have left behind better words than what you said, and more correct opinions than what you saw, and more beautiful commands than what you brought, and wiser sermons than what you described. Job had a better right and covenant over you than what you described. Do you know, O elders, the right of whom you have diminished?’ Whose sanctity did you violate? Who is the man you blamed and accused? And you do not know, O elders, that Job is the prophet of God and His chosen one and the best of the people of the earth on this day of yours. God chose him for His revelation, and selected him for Himself, and entrusted him with his prophethood. Then you did not know, and God did not inform you, that he was displeased with any of the honor with which He honored him since He gave him what He gave him until this day of yours. If the affliction is what has disgraced him in your eyes and placed him in your souls, then you have known that God tests the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. Then he is not of this status with God, nor in prophethood, nor in self-interest, nor in virtue, nor in honor, except that he is a brother whom you loved in the manner of the companions. It would not be appropriate for the wise to reproach his brother when afflicted, nor to reproach him for the calamity with what he does not know, and he is distressed and sad, but he has mercy on him and weeps with him, and seeks forgiveness for him, and is sad for his sadness, and guides him to the right path in his matter, and he is not wise nor righteous from Ignorance of this, so be careful, you old men, about yourselves. He said: Then he turned to Job, peace be upon him, and said: There was in the greatness and majesty of God and the mention of death what would cut your tongue, break your heart, and make you forget your arguments. Did you not know, O Job, that God has servants whom His fear silenced without defect or dumbness? They are the eloquent, articulate, noble, and intelligent ones, who work for God and His verses. But when they mention the greatness of God, their tongues become cut off, their skins shudder, their hearts break, and their minds go astray out of reverence for God, honor, and veneration. So when they wake up from that, they race to God with righteous deeds, preparing themselves with the oppressors and sinners, and they are the most pure and innocent, and with the negligent and the negligent. And they are wise and strong, but they do not consider much too much for God, nor are they satisfied with little for God, nor do they guide to Him with deeds. They are terrified, frightened, grieved, humbled, fearful, submissive, and confessing. Whenever you see them, O Job. Ayyub said: God plants wisdom with mercy in the heart of the young and the old. When it grows in the heart, God reveals it on the tongue. Wisdom does not come from age, youth, or length of experience. If God makes a servant wise in fasting, his status with the wise will not fall, and they will see the light of honor from God upon him. But you have become proud of yourselves, and you thought that you have howled with your goodness. So there you have transgressed and become arrogant. If you had looked between you and your Lord, and then believed in yourselves, you would have found faults that God has covered with the well-being that He has clothed you with. But today I have become without an opinion or a word with you. I used to have my words heard, my right known, fair with my opponent, subduing those who today subdue me, and my position is feared. Despite that, men listen to me and respect me. But today my hope has been cut off, my caution has been lifted, my family has grown tired of me, and my relatives have disobeyed me. My acquaintances have disowned me, my friends have turned away from me, my companions have cut me off, my family have disbelieved in me, I have denied my rights, and I have forgotten my good deeds. I cry out, but they do not cry out to me. I apologize, but they do not excuse me. It is His judgment that has humiliated me, made me weak, and made me miserable. It is His authority that has made me sick and made my body thin. If my Lord were to remove the awe that is in my chest, and set my tongue free so that I could speak at full capacity, then it would be appropriate for the servant to argue for himself, I would hope that He would punish me for what I am in. But He has thrown me aside, and He is exalted above me. He sees me, but I do not see Him. He hears me, but I do not hear Him. He has not looked at me and had mercy on me, nor has He approached me nor brought me near. So I present my excuse, and I speak of my innocence, and I plead for myself. When he said, “He was humiliated like Job and his companions with him,” a cloud overshadowed him until his companions thought it was a punishment. Then he was called from him, and it was said to him: “O Job, God says: Here I am, I have come near to you, and I have always been close to you, so arise and present your excuse that you claimed, and speak of your innocence, and argue for yourself, and tighten your garment.” Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Ibn Askar, on the authority of Ismail, to the end of it, and he added to it: “And My mercy has preceded My wrath, so strike with your foot, this is a cool bath and a drink in which is your cure, and I have given you your family, and the like of them with them, and your wealth and the like of it with it.” And they claimed: And the like of it with it so that it may be a sign for those who come after you, and so that it may be a lesson for those who are afflicted. Then he went out and sat down, and his wife came looking for him in his bed, but she did not find him, so she stood up as if she were in a state of bewilderment, then she said: O servant of God, do you know about the afflicted man who was here? He said: No, then he smiled, so I recognized him by his laughter, and embraced him. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: So I told Abdullah ibn Abbas his story and her embrace of him, and Abdullah said: By the One in Whose hand is Abdullah’s soul, she did not leave his embrace until all of their wealth and children had passed by her. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: I heard some of those who mentioned the hadith about him that he called her when she asked about him and said to her: Do you recognize him when you saw him? She said: Yes, why do I not know him? He smiled and said: Here I am, and God has relieved me of what I was in. At that point, she embraced him. Wahb said: Then God revealed in His oath to strike her for what she spoke to, that And take in your hand a bunch of grass and strike with it and do not break your oath (Surah Sad: 44) meaning your oath has been fulfilled. God the Most High says: “Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who frequently turned back [to God]” (Surah Sad: 44). God says: And We gave him his family and the like thereof with them as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding (Surah Sad: 43). Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Job remained lying on a dustbin for seven years and months, not asking God to relieve what was wrong with him. He said: There is no creature on the face of the earth more honorable to God than Job. They claim that some people said: If the Lord of this had a need for him, He would not have done this to him. At that point, he prayed. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Abu Bakr remained in charge of the scavenger hunt for the Children of Israel for seven years and months, and the animals would attack him. Muhammad bin Ishaq told me: Yahya bin Ma’in told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: Ayyub did not eat, but rather he would bring out something like a woman’s breast and then he would lick it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Mukhallad bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Hajjaj, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan: One of them added to the other, he said: God gave Job wealth, and made it abundant for him and for him women, cows, sheep and camels, and the enemy of God, Satan, was asked: Are you able to tempt Job? He said: O Lord, Job has become in a world of wealth and children, and he cannot help but thank You, but give me power over his wealth and children, and you will see how he obeys Me and disobeys You. K said: So give him power over his wealth and children. He said: So he would bring his livestock from his wealth of sheep and burn them in the fire. Then Job would come, while he was praying, imitating a shepherd, and K would say: O Job, you pray to your Lord, God has not left you anything from your livestock from the sheep except that He burned it in the fire. I was away and I came to inform you. He said: So Job would say: O God, You gave, and You took, as long as my soul remains I thank You for Your good trial, and he would not be able to do anything of what he wanted. Then he would bring his livestock of cows and burn them in the fire. Then Job would come and say that, and Job would respond to him in the same way. He said: And he did the same with the camels until he had nothing left of his livestock until he demolished the house on his son. Then he said: O Job, God sent upon your son someone who demolished houses on them until they perished. So Job said the same thing. He said: My Lord, this is when You have done me all good. Before today, the love of money occupied me during the day, and the love of my son occupied me at night out of compassion for them. So now I empty my hearing and my sight, my night and my day with remembrance and praise, sanctification and glorification. So the enemy of God departs from him without having obtained from him anything that he wanted. He said: Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: How did you see Job? Iblis said: Job knows that you will return his wealth and children to him. But give me power over his body, so that if harm befalls him therein, he will obey me and disobey you. He said: So he was given power over his body, so he came to him and blew into him a blast that caused a sore from his horn to his foot. He said: Then calamity after calamity befell him, until he was carried and placed on a garbage dump for the Children of Israel. He had no wealth, children, friends, or anyone to come near him except his wife. She was patient with him sincerely, and she would bring him food, and praise God with him when he praised Him. And Job, despite that, did not cease to remember God, and to praise and extol God, and to be patient with what God had afflicted him with. Al-Hasan said: Then Iblis, the enemy of God, cried out a cry in which he gathered his soldiers from all corners of the earth, fearing Job’s patience. They gathered around him and said to him: You have gathered us, what is the matter with you? What has made you tired? He said: This servant has exhausted me, whom I asked my Lord to give me power over his wealth and children, so I did not leave him wealth or children, and he only increased in patience and praise and thanks to God. Then I gave power over his body and left it as a sore lying on the rubbish dump of the Children of Israel, and none acknowledged it except his wife. I have disgraced myself before my Lord, so I sought help from you, so help me against him. He said: They said to him: Where is your cunning? Where is your knowledge with which you destroyed those who came before? He said: All of that has been invalidated in Job, so advise me. They said: We advise you. Did you see Adam when you expelled him from Paradise, from where did you come to him? He said: From his wife. They said: What about Job from his wife, for he cannot disobey her, and no one comes near him except her? He said: You have hit the nail on the head. So he went until he came to his wife while she was giving charity, and he appeared to her in the form of a man, and he said: Where is your husband, O servant of God? She said: It is that which scratches his sores, and the animals move around his body. When he heard it, he hoped that it was a word of distress, so it fell into her heart, and whispered to her, and reminded her of the blessings, wealth, and animals that she had been in, and reminded her of Job’s beauty and youth, and the harm that he was in, and that this would never end for them. Al-Hasan said: So she screamed, and when she screamed, he knew that she had screamed and was distressed, so he brought her a goat and said: Let Job slaughter this for me and he will be healed. He said: So she came screaming, O Job, O Job, until when will your Lord torment you? Will He not have mercy on you? The livestock? The money? Where are the children? Where is the friend? Your beautiful color has changed, and has become like ashes? Your beautiful body. Who has worn out and the beasts have wandered in it? Slaughter this young goat and rest. Job said: The enemy of God has come to you, breathed into you, and found in you gentleness, and you answered him: Woe to you! Who gave it to me? She said: God. He said: How long did He give us enjoyment of it? She said: Eighty years. He said: Since when did God afflict us with this trial with which He has afflicted us? She said: Seven years and some months. He said: Woe to you! By God, you have not been just, nor have you been fair to your Lord. Why did you not have patience so that we may be in this trial with which our Lord has afflicted us for eighty years, just as we were in prosperity for eighty years? By God, if God heals me, I will flog you a hundred lashes. You have ordered me to slaughter for other than God your food and drink that you bring me unlawfully. I will not taste what you bring me after that. Since you have said this to me, then go away from me, so that I may not see you. So he expelled her, and she left. Then Satan said: This man has prepared himself for eighty years for this affliction that he is in, but he was overcome and rejected. Job looked at his wife and expelled her, and he had no food, no drink, and no friend. Al-Hasan said: Two men passed by him while he was in that state. By God, there was no one on the face of the earth that day more honorable to God than Job. One of the two men said to his companion: If God had a need for this, He would not have brought him to this. Job had not heard anything that was more difficult for him than this word. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair, who said: Ayoub had two brothers, so they came to him and stood from a distance, unable to approach him because of his stench. One of them said to his companion: If God had known any good in Ayoub, He would not have afflicted him with what he saw. He said: Ayoub was never so distressed by anything that befell him as he was by a man’s words. Ayoub said: O God, if You know that I have never spent a night full while I know where someone is hungry, then believe me. So he believed me, and they were listening. Then he said: O God, if You know that I have never worn two shirts while I know where someone is naked, then believe me. So he believed me, and they were listening. He said: Then he fell down prostrating. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Mukhallad bin Al-Hussein told me, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: So he said: O Lord, indeed harm has befallen me. Then he referred that to his Lord, and He said: And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, he said: So it was said to him: Raise your head, for your prayer has been answered. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Mukhallad, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the hadith of one of them entered into the other. They said: So it was said to him, Strike with your foot, this is a cool bath and a drink (p. 42). So he struck with his foot and a spring gushed forth, so he washed from it, and nothing of his illness remained apparent on him except that it fell off. So God removed all pain and all sickness, and his youth and beauty returned to him, better than it had been and more excellent than it had been. Then he struck with his foot and another spring gushed forth, so he drank from it, and nothing of his illness remained in his body except that it came out. So he stood up healthy, and he was clothed in a garment. He said: So he began to look around and did not see anything of his family and wealth except that God had weakened it for him, until, by God, he repeated to us that the water with which he had washed had scattered on his chest like golden locusts. He said: So he began to hold them in his hand, and God revealed to him: O Job, have I not enriched you? He said: Yes, but it is your blessing, who can be satisfied with it? He said: So he went out and sat on a prominent place, then his wife said: Tell me, if he expelled me to whom did he eat it? Should I leave it to die of hunger or be lost and eaten by wild beasts? I will return to it. So she returned, and there was no sweeping place to be seen, nor was it in the same condition that it was, and things had changed, so she began to walk around when the sweeping place was and cry, and that was in the eyes of Ayoub. She said: And she was afraid to go to the owner of the estate and ask about him, so Ayoub sent to her and called her, and said: What do you want, O servant of God? So she cried and said: I wanted that afflicted one who was rejected on the sweeping place, I do not know if he was lost or what he did? Ayoub said to her: What happened to you? So she cried and said: My husband, have you seen him? And she cried that he was here. He said: And would you recognize him if you saw him? She said: Is it hidden from anyone who saw him? Then she began to look at him and she was afraid of him, then she said: He was the most similar of God’s creation to you, because he was healthy. He said: I am Job, whom you ordered to slaughter Satan, and I obeyed God and disobeyed Satan, so I called upon God and He returned to me what you see. Al-Hasan said: Then God had mercy on her because of her patience with Him in the face of the affliction, and He ordered him, to make things easier for her, to take a group of trees and strike them with one blow, to make things easier for her because of her patience with Him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And Job, when he cried out to his Lord, ‘Verily, distress has seized me’… until the end of the two verses, for when Satan touched him with hardship and torment, God made him forget to supplicate to Him, so that He would remove the distress that was upon him. However, he used to remember God often, and the affliction in God only increased his desire and good faith. Then when the appointed time came and God decreed that He would remove the distress that was upon him, He permitted him to supplicate and made it easy for him. Before that, the Blessed and Exalted used to say: It is not appropriate for My servant Job to supplicate to Me, and then I would not answer him. So when he supplicated, He answered him, and He replaced everything that he had lost with double, He returned to him his family and the like thereof with them, and He praised him and said: “Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who frequently turned back [to God]” (Surah Sad: 44). The people of interpretation differed about the family that God mentioned in His statement, And We gave him his family and a like number with them. Are they the family that he was given in this world, or is that the promise that God promised Job that He would do to him in the Hereafter? Some of them said: God only gave Job in this world the like of his family that perished, for they will not return to him in this world, and God only promised Job that He would give them to him in the Hereafter. Abu al-Sa’ib Salim ibn Janadah told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, who said: Mujahid sent a man called Qasim to Ikrimah asking him about the statement of God to Job, And We gave him his family and the like of them with them. He said: It was said to him: Your family is yours in the Hereafter, so if you wish, We will hasten them for you in this world, and if you wish, they will be yours in the Hereafter, and We will give you the like of them in this world. He said: They will be for me in the Hereafter, and I will be given the like of them in this world. He said: So he returned to Mujahid and said, He is right. Others said: Rather, he returned them to him in their entirety, and gave him the same amount along with them. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Hakam bin Salim narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Masoud: And We gave him his family and the like thereof with them. He said: His family in person. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, when Job prayed, God answered him and replaced everything he had lost with two times more. He returned his family to him and the same number with them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And We gave him his family and the like thereof with them (p. 43). He said: He brought them back to life in person, and returned to him the like thereof. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We gave him his family and the like thereof with them, he said: It was said to him: If you wish, We will revive them for you, and if you wish, they will be yours in the Hereafter, and you will be given the like thereof in this world. So he chose that they should be in the Hereafter and the like thereof in this world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We gave him his family and the like thereof with them. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: God revived his family in person, and added to them the like thereof. Others said: Rather, he gave him the example of his offspring, his wealth, which he returned to him, and his family. As for the family and wealth, he returned them to him. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Hasan: And the like of them with them. He said: Of their descendants. His saying, mercy is in the accusative case, meaning: We did that to them out of mercy from Us to him. His saying, and a reminder to the worshippers, means: And a reminder to the worshippers of their Lord. We did that to him so that they would take heed from it, and know that God may test His friends and those of His servants whom He loves in this world with various types of affliction in themselves, their families, and their wealth, not to degrade them, but as a test from Him to him so that he may attain, through his patience with it, his acceptance of it, and his good faith, the station that He, the Blessed and Exalted, has prepared for him of honor with Him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b Al-Qurazi, regarding his statement, A mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers, he said: Any believer who is afflicted with a calamity and mentions what afflicted Job, it will be said: Someone better than us, a prophet from among the prophets, has been afflicted.
21:85: God Almighty means by Ishmael: Ishmael, son of Abraham, who fulfilled his promise, and by Idris: Enoch, and by Dhu al-Kifl: a man who took responsibility for some of the people, either a prophet or a righteous king, to do some work, and then someone took it on after him, so God praised him for his good fulfillment of what he took responsibility for, and made him one of those counted among His servants, with those who praised his patience. He mentioned the narration about them: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated: Mu'ammil narrated: Sufyan narrated: Al-A'mash narrated: Al-Munhal bin Amr narrated: Abdullah bin Al-Harith narrated that a prophet said: Who will guarantee that he will fast during the day and pray at night and will not get angry? A young man stood up and said: I will. He said: Sit down. Then he came back and said: Who will guarantee that he will fast during the night and will not get angry? That young man stood up and said: I will. He said: You will pray at night and fast during the day and will not get angry. Then that prophet died, and that young man sat in his place to judge between the people, but he did not get angry. Then Satan came to him in the form of a man to anger him while he was fasting and wanted to take a nap, so he knocked hard on the door and said: Who is this? He said: A man who has a need. So he sent another with him, but he said: I am not satisfied with this one. So he went out to him and took him by the hand and he went with him, until when he was in the market, he left him and went away, and he was called Dhul-Kifl. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Affan bin Muslim told us: Wahib told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: When Al-Yasa’ grew old, he said: If only I could appoint a man as my successor over the people to work over them during my lifetime, so that I could see how he works. A man whom the eye despised stood up and said: Me. He said: Do you fast during the day and pray at night, and do not get angry? He said: Yes. He said: So he turned them back that day and said the same thing about the other night. The people remained silent and that man stood up and said: Me. He appointed him as his successor. Iblis began to say to the devils: Go to so-and-so, but he exhausted them. He said: Leave me and him. He came to him in the form of an old, poor man. He came to him when he went to bed for the afternoon nap, and he did not sleep day or night except for that nap. He knocked on the door and said: Who is this? He said: An old man who has been wronged.
