He said: So he got up and opened the door and began to tell him the story, saying: There is a dispute between me and my people, and they have wronged me, and they did this and that to me. So he kept on talking to him for a long time, until it was time for the afternoon prayer and the midday meal. He said: When you go, come to me so that I may take your right for you. So he went and went, and was in his council, and he began to look to see if he could see the old man, but he did not see him, so he began to seek him out. When the next day came, he began to judge between the people and wait for him, but he did not see him. When he returned for the midday meal and went to bed, he came to him and knocked on the door, and he said: Who is this? He said: The old oppressed man. So he opened the door for him and said: Didn’t I tell you that when you sit, come to me? He said: They are the most wicked people. If they know that you are sitting, they say: We will give you your right, and if you stand, they deny me. He said: Go, and when you go, come to me. He said: So he missed the siesta, so he went to look but did not see him, and drowsiness overcame him, so he said to some of his family: Do not let anyone approach this door until I sleep, for sleep overcame me. When that hour came, he came and the man said to him: Behind you, so he said: I went to him yesterday and told him my situation. He said: By God, we were ordered not to let anyone approach it. When he became tired, he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed through it, and behold, he was in the house, and behold, he was knocking on the door. He said: The man woke up and said: O so-and-so, did I not order you? He said: By God, as for those before me, you were not given access, so look from where you came. He said: So he went to the door, and behold, it was locked as he had locked it, and behold, he was with him in the house, so he recognized him and said: Enemy of God? He said: Yes, you exhausted me in everything, so I did what you see to anger you. So he called him Dhul-Kifl, because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And Dhul-Kifl, he said: A righteous man who was not a prophet, guaranteed to the prophet of his people that he would take care of his people’s affairs, establish them for them, and judge between them with justice, so he did that, and he was called Dhul-Kifl. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: And He judges between them with justice. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Abu Ma`shar narrated: Muhammad ibn Qays said: The Children of Israel had a righteous king. He became arrogant and gathered his people and said: Who among you will guarantee me this kingdom of mine, on condition that he fasts during the day, prays at night, and judges between the Children of Israel according to what God has revealed? No one stood up except that young man. He said: So he disdained him. When it was the third time, he said the same thing, and no one stood up except that young man. He said: Go ahead. So he was left with his kingdom. The young man stood up one night, and when morning came, he began to judge between the Children of Israel. When it was noon, he went in to take a nap, and Satan came to him in the form of a man from the children of Adam, and pulled his garment, and said: Do you sleep while the disputants are at your door? He said: When it is evening, come to me. He said: So he waited for him in the evening, but he did not come. When it was noon, he went in to take a nap, pulled his garment, and said: Do you sleep while the disputants are at your door? He said: I told you: Come to me in the evening, but you did not come. Come to me in the evening. When it was evening, he waited for him, but he did not come. When he entered to take a nap, he pulled his garment and said: Are you sleeping while the opponents are at your door? He said: Tell me who you are. If you were human, you would have heard what you said. He said: He is the devil. I have come to capture you, but God protected you from me. So he judged between the Children of Israel according to what God revealed for a long time. He is Dhul-Kifl. He was called Dhul-Kifl because he took responsibility for the kingdom. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, he said while he was addressing the al-Nas 114:Indeed, Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was a righteous servant who took care of the work of a righteous man when he died. He used to pray to God a hundred times every day, so God praised him well for taking care of him. Ibn Humayd narrated: Al-Hakam narrated: Amr narrated: As for Dhul-Kifl, he was a king over the Children of Israel. When death approached him, he said: Who will guarantee that the Children of Israel will suffice me, and will not get angry, and will pray one hundred prayers every day? Dhul-Kifl said: I will. So Dhul-Kifl began to judge between the people, and when he finished, he prayed one hundred prayers. Then Satan tricked him and gave him time until he had judged between the people, and finished his prayer, and went to bed and slept. Then Satan came to his door and began to knock on it. So the devil came out to him and said: You have wronged me and done to me. So he gave him his ring and said: Go and bring me your companion, and waited for him. But the other one delayed him until he knew that he had fallen asleep and gone to bed. Then he came to the door also in order to anger him, and he began to knock on it and scratched his own face, and blood flowed. So the devil came out to him and said: What is the matter with you? He said: He did not follow me, and I struck him and he did that. So Dhul-Kifl seized him and denied what he had done. Then he said: Tell me who you are? He took him violently. He said: Tell him who he is. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And Dhul-Kifl, he said: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari said: Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was responsible for the prayer of a man who used to pray one hundred prayers every day, so he fulfilled it, so he was responsible for his prayer, and that is why he was called Dhul-Kifl. And Ismail, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl were placed in the accusative case, in apposition to Job, then he resumed with his statement, all, so he said, all of the patient ones, and the meaning of the statement is: All of them are among the people of patience in what befalls them for the sake of God.
21:86: And His statement, And We admitted them into Our mercy, for they were among the righteous. God Almighty says: And We admitted Ishmael, Idris, and Dhul-Kifl, and the ha and mim refer to them. Into Our mercy, for they were among the righteous. He says: They are among those who were righteous, so they obeyed God and did what He commanded them.
21:87: God Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, Dhul-Nun, meaning the owner of the fish, and the fish is the whale. Dhul-Nun is Yunus bin Matta, and we have mentioned his story in Surah Yunus in a way that makes it unnecessary to mention him in this place. And His statement, When he went away in anger, means when he went away in anger. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his leaving in anger, and about whom he left, and against whom he was angry. Some of them said: He left his people and them in anger. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And Dhul-Nun, when he went off in anger, meaning: He was angry with his people. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, When he went away in anger, as for his anger, it was against his people. Others said: He left his people, angry with his Lord, when He removed the punishment from them after He had promised them. He mentioned who said that, and he mentioned the reason for his Lord’s anger at what they said. Ibn Hamid narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God sent him, meaning Yunus, to the people of his village, and they rejected what he had brought them and refused him. When they did that, God revealed to him: I am sending them punishment on such and such a day, so go out from among them. So inform his people of the punishment that God has promised them. They said: Look at him, for if he goes out from among you, then by God, what He has promised you will happen. When the night in which they were promised punishment came, in the morning, he set out early and the people saw him. They went out of the village to a clearing in their land, and they separated every animal from its young. Then they cried out to God and asked Him to excuse them, so He excused them. Yunus waited for report about the village and its people, until someone passed by him and said: What happened to the people of the village? He said: They did so because their prophet left their midst. They knew that he had fulfilled his promise of punishment to them. So they left their village to a clearing on the ground, then they separated every female child from her child, and they cried out to God and repented to Him. So He accepted it from them and delayed the punishment from them. He said: Then Yunus said at that time and became angry: By God, I will never return to them as a liar. I promised them punishment in one day, then it was turned away from them, and he went on his way in anger. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Awf told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: It has reached me that when Yunus committed the sin, he went away angry with his Lord, and Satan caused him to slip. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of Abu Zaydah, on the authority of Mujalid bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement, When he went away in anger, he said: In anger with his Lord. Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Abdul Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Salamah, and he added to it: He said: So Yunus went out to see the torment, but he did not see anything. He said: They have tested me with a lie. So he went away, angry with his Lord, until he came to the sea. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Rabia ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: I heard him say: Yunus ibn Matta was a righteous servant, but his character was narrow. When the burdens of prophethood were placed upon him, and it is a burden that only a few can bear, he collapsed under it as a quarter collapses under its load. So he threw it out in front of him and fled from it. God says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will (al-Ahqaf 46:35), So be patient over the decision of your Lord, and be not like the companion of the fish (al-Qalam 68:48): meaning, do not accept My command as I accept it. This statement, I mean the statement of the one who said: He left his people in anger with his Lord, is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, because the statement So he thought that We would not have power over him indicates that, and that those who interpreted it as him leaving in anger with his people, only claimed that they did that out of their disapproval that a prophet would be angry with his Lord, and because they thought it was too great for him. And their saying that he left in anger with his people has entered into a matter greater than what they disapproved of, because those who said: He left in anger with his Lord, differed about the reason for his leaving in this way. Some of them said: He only did what he did out of dislike to be among a people who had experienced him breaking his promise to them, and he was ashamed of them, and he did not know the reason by which he averted the calamity from them. And some of those who said this statement said: It was from the morals of his people whom he left, to kill those who had experienced him lying, hoping that they would kill him because he promised them punishment, but what he promised them did not come upon them. We mentioned the narration about that in Surat Yunus, so we disliked repeating it in this place. Others said: Rather, his Lord was angry because he was ordered to go to a people to warn them of His punishment and call them to Him. So he asked his Lord to give him time, so that he could prepare to go to them. So he was told: The matter is faster than that. And he did not wait until he wanted to wait until he took a sandal to wear it. So he was told something similar to the first statement. And he was a man of narrow build. He said: My Lord hastened me to take a sandal. So he went away angry. Among those who mentioned this saying about him: Al-Hasan Al-Basri. Al-Harith told me that. He said: Al-Hussein bin Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on his authority. Abu Ja`far said: There is nothing in either of these two statements describing the Prophet of God, Yunus, peace be upon him, except that it is less than what was described by those who said: He went in anger with his people, because his departure from his people in anger with them, and God Almighty had commanded him to stay among them, to convey his message to them, and warn them of his wrath and punishment, for their abandonment of belief in him, and working in obedience to him, there is no doubt that there is what is in it, and if it were not that he, peace be upon him, had done what those who described him as committing a sin said, God Almighty would not have punished him with the punishment that He mentioned in His Book, and described him with the description that He described him with, and said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: And be not like the companion of the fish when he cried out in anguish (al-Qalam 68:48) and said: “And the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy. And had he not been of those who glorify God, he would have remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection” (al-Saffat 37:142-144). And his saying, So he thought that We would not have power over him, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: Its meaning is: So he thought that We would not punish him by restricting him, from their saying, I restricted someone: if you restricted him, as God Almighty said And whoever’s provision is restricted, let him spend from what God has given him al-Talaq 65:7. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He thought that We would not have power over him, meaning: He thought that the punishment that befell him would not overtake him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He thought that We would not have power over him. He said: He thought that We would not impose punishment or affliction on him, so what did he do to his people in his anger when he became angry with them and his flight, and his punishment is the taking of the letter nun from him. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse, So he thought that We would not have power over him. He said: So he thought that We would not punish him for his sin. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said: Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said: Shu’bah told me, on the authority of Mujahid, and he did not mention the ruling in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So he thought that We would not have power over him, he said: He says: He thought that We would not punish him. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Al-Kalbi: He thought that We would not have power over him. They said: He thought that We would not impose punishment on him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, So he thought that We would not have power over him, meaning: He thought that God would not decree punishment or affliction upon him in His anger with which He was angry at his people and his separation from them. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So he thought that We would not have power over him, he said, the affliction that befell him. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He thought that his Lord was unable to do anything to him, so He would not be able to do anything to him. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Awf told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: It has reached me that Yunus did not commit a sin. He set out angry with his Lord, and Satan made him slip until he thought that he would not be able to defeat him. He said: He had a history of worship and glorification, but God refused to leave him to Satan, so he took him and threw him into the belly of the whale. He remained in the belly of the whale for forty days and nights, and God held him back and did not kill him there. He repented to his Lord in the belly of the whale and reviewed himself. He said: Glory be to You, indeed, I was among the wrongdoers. He said: So God extracted him from the belly of the whale by His mercy, because of his past worship and glorification, and made him among the righteous. Awf said: It has reached me that he said in his supplication: And I have built for you a mosque in a place that no one before me has built. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: So he thought that We would not have power over him. And he had a history of worship and glorification, so God helped him with it and did not leave him to Satan. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Iyas ibn Muawiyah al-Madani, that whenever Yunus was mentioned in his presence, and his statement, So he thought that We would not decree anything against him, Iyas would say: So why did he flee? Others said: Rather, it means a question, and its interpretation is: Do you think that We will not be able to do anything to him? Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, So he thought that We would not decree power over him, he said: This is a question, and regarding his statement, So what good are vows? (al-Qamar 54:5), he said: It is also a question. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting this, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: What he meant by it is: So Jonah thought that We would not imprison him and make things difficult for him, as a punishment for him for angering his Lord. We said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the word, because it is not permissible to attribute it to disbelief, and he chose it for his prophethood, and his description of him as thinking that his Lord is unable to do what He wanted for him, and is not able to do it, is a description of him as being ignorant of the power of God, and that is a description of him as a disbeliever, and it is not permissible for anyone to describe him with that. As for what Ibn Zayd said, it is a statement that if there was evidence in the speech that it is a good question, but there is no evidence in it that this is so, and the Arabs do not delete from speech something that they need, except that they leave evidence that it is intended in the speech, so if there is no evidence in his saying so he thought that We will not be able to do it that what is intended by it is a question, as Ibn Zayd said: it was known that it is not so, and since these two aspects are invalid, the third is correct and it is what we said. And his saying, Then he called out in the darkness, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of these darknesses. Some of them said: He meant by them the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, Then he called out in the darkness, he said: the darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. And Ibn Jurayj also said the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He called out in the darkness: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale: “There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Salami told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Muhammad bin Rafa’ah told us, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ka’b say about this verse, Then he called out in the darkness, he said: The darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then he called out in the darkness, he said: The darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then he called out in the darkness. He said: The darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. Others said: What he meant by that was that he called out in the darkness of the belly of a whale in the belly of another whale in the sea. They said: So that was in the darkness. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d: Then he called out in the darkness. He said: God inspired the whale not to harm its flesh or bones, then the whale swallowed another whale. He said: Then he called out in the darkness. He said: The darkness of the whale, then another whale, then the darkness of the sea. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement about this is to say: God informed us about Jonah that He called out to him in the darkness, “There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.” There is no doubt that by one of the darknesses He meant the belly of the whale, and by the other: the darkness of the sea, and there is a difference in the third. It is possible that the third is the darkness of the night, and it is possible that it is the whale being in the belly of another whale, and there is no evidence to indicate which of these is which, so there is no statement about this that is more worthy of the truth than submission to the apparent meaning of the revelation. And his saying: There is no god but You, glory be to You, he says: Jonah called out with this saying, confessing his sin, repenting from his mistake, Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers, in my disobedience to You. Ibn Hamid also told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “He called out in the darkness, ‘There is no god but You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.’” Confessing his sin and repenting from his mistake. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Abu Ma’shar said: Muhammad bin Qais said: His statement: There is no god but You, glory be to You I did not do anything and I did not worship anyone but You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers when I disobeyed You. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Awf Al-A’rabi, he said: When Yunus was in the belly of the whale, he thought that he had died, then he moved his leg, and when it moved he prostrated in his place, then he called out: O Lord, I have made for You a place of prostration in a place where no one has made. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me from someone who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God wanted to imprison Jonah in the belly of the whale, God revealed to the whale: Take him, and do not scratch his flesh or break his bones. So it took him and then plunged with him to his home in the sea. When it reached the bottom of the sea, Jonah heard a sound, so he said to himself: What is this? So God revealed to him while he was in the belly of the whale: This is the glorification of the sea creatures. So he glorified while he was in the belly of the whale, and the angels heard his glorification, and they said: O our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land. He said: That is My servant Jonah. He disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea. They said: The righteous servant from whom a righteous deed ascended to You every day and night? He said: Yes. He said: Then they interceded for him, and he ordered the whale to throw him up on the shore, as God Almighty said: “And he was sick.”
21:88: God Almighty says: So We answered Jonah’s supplication to Us, when he called upon Us in the belly of the whale, and We saved him from the distress he was in by imprisoning him in the belly of the whale, and his distress was due to his sin and his guilt. And thus do We save the believers. God Almighty says: Just as We saved Jonah from the distress of being imprisoned in the belly of the whale in the sea when he called upon Us, thus do We save the believers from their distress when they seek help from Us and call upon Us. The effect came in a similar manner to what we said about it. Who said that? Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Salih narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Bishr bin Mansour narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, saying: I heard Saad bin Malik say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The name of God by which He is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives, is the supplication of Yunus bin Matta. He said: So I said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for Yunus bin Matta, or for the entirety of the Muslims? He said: It is specifically for Yunus bin Matta, and for the believers in general if they supplicate with it. Have you not heard the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted: “Then he cried out in the darknesses, ‘There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.’ So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.” This is God’s condition for whoever calls upon Him with it. The reciters differed in his saying, We will save the believers. The reciters of the regions read it that way, except for Asim, with two noons, the second of which is silent, from Anjinah, “nanjihi.” And they only read it that way, and its writing in the copies of the Qur’an with one noon, because if it had been read with one noon and a shaddah on the jeem, meaning that whose agent is not named, then the believers would be in the nominative case, and they are in the accusative case in the copies of the Qur’an. And if it had been read with one noon and a light jeem, it would have been for the believers, and they would have been in the nominative case, and it would have been necessary with that that his saying: (Naja) is written with an alif because it is one of the letters with a waw, and in the Qur’ans it is written with a ya. If someone were to say: How can this be written with one noon, when you know that the rule for that when it is read as nanji is to write it with two noons? It is said: Because when the second noon was still, and the still one was not apparent on the tongue, it was deleted as they did with illa, so they deleted the noon from in because of its concealment, since it was assimilated into the lam from la, and ‘Asim read that Naji al-Mu’minin with one noon, and the emphasis on the jim, and the sukun on the ya’, if ‘Asim’s reading of that is based on the Arabs’ saying: The darb struck Zayd, so he referred to the source which is the escape, and made the report, I mean the report of what the doer of which was not named, the believers, as if he meant: And likewise the escape saved the believers, so he referred to the escape, so that is a view, although another view is more correct, otherwise the one who read it according to what he read it according to what the reciters read it on is adding another noon that is not in the Mushaf, so he thought that it was an addition of what is not in the Mushaf, and he did not know a view to which to refer it for its deletion. Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading, which I do not permit other than that, according to us, is what the readers of the regions do, which is to read it with two noons and to soften the jim, due to the consensus of the authority among the readers on it, and the error of it is contrary to it.
21:89: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, Zechariah, when he called upon his Lord, My Lord, leave me not alone, alone, having no children or descendants, and You are the best of inheritors. He said: So provide me with an heir from the family of Jacob who will inherit me. Then He referred the matter back to God, saying: And You are the best of inheritors. God Almighty says: So We answered Zechariah’s prayer, and We gave him John as a son and an heir to inherit him, and We made his wife good for him. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the righteousness that God Almighty meant by His saying: And We made his wife righteous for him. Some of them said: She was barren, so He made her righteous by making her fertile. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Hatim bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Sakhr, on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Saeed, regarding his statement: And We made his wife good for him, he said: She was not able to bear children. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement: And We made his wife good for him, he said: We gave him her child. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We made his wife good for him: She was barren, so God made her fertile and gave him John through her. Others said: She had bad manners, but God made her better for him by granting her good manners. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about that is to say: God made his wife good for Zachariah, as God Almighty informed us by making her fertile and of good character, because all of that is from the meanings of His making her good, and God Almighty did not specify some of that over others in His Book, nor on the tongue of His Messenger, nor did He place any indication of that in particular, so it is general unless something comes that must be accepted that it is intended for some over others. And His statement: Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds God says: Indeed, those whom We named, meaning Zachariah, his wife, and John, used to hasten to do good deeds in obedience to Us, and to do that which brings them closer to Us. And His statement: And they used to call upon Us in hope and fear God the Most High says: And they used to worship Us in hope and fear. And by supplication in this place He means worship, as He said: And I will leave you and what you invoke besides God, and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I will not be, in the invocation of my Lord, unhappy (Maryam 19:48). And by His statement: in hope He means that they used to worship Him out of desire for what they hoped from Him of His mercy and grace, and in fear meaning out of fear of His punishment and chastisement, for abandoning His worship and committing His disobedience. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, They used to hasten to do good deeds and call upon Us in hope and fear. He said: In hope of God’s mercy and in fear of God’s punishment. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And they call upon Us in hope and fear, he said: Out of fear and greed. He said: And it is not appropriate for one of them to separate from the other. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions read it as raghban wa rahban with a fatha on the ghain and the ha’ from raghb and rahab. There was a difference of opinion regarding this from Al-A’mash, and it was narrated from him that he agreed with the reciters in this. It was narrated from him that he read it as raghban wa rahban with a damma on the ra’ in both letters and a sukoon on the ghain and the ha’. The correct reading in this regard is what the readers of the countries do, which is the opening in both letters. And His saying: And they were humble before Us, means: And they were humble and submissive before Us, and they were not too proud to worship Us and supplicate to Us.
21:90: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “So We responded to him and granted him John and made his wife sound for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.”
21:91: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention she who guarded her chastity, meaning Mary, daughter of Imran. What He means by His statement: guarded is that she protected and prevented her chastity from what God had forbidden her to do in it. There is a difference of opinion about the joy that God Almighty meant that she protected him from. Some of them said: He meant by that the relief of her soul that she protected from immorality. Others said: He meant by that the pocket of our armor that she prevented Gabriel from it before she knew that he was the Messenger of her Lord, and before she established knowledge of him. They said: What is indicated by his saying: Then We breathed into her and that is followed by his saying: And she who guarded her chastity they said: And it was known from that that the meaning of the statement: And she who guarded her pocket Then We breathed into her of Our spirit. Abu Ja`far said: The one who has the better of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of this, in our view, is the one who says: She protected her private parts from immorality, because that is the more likely of its two meanings for him, and what is more apparent in the apparent meaning of the statement: Then We breathed into her of Our spirit means: Then We breathed into the pocket of her armor of Our spirit. We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed regarding the meaning of his statement: Then We breathed into her in other places. The more correct opinion regarding this in what has passed is that there is no need to repeat it in this place. And His statement: And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds means: And We made Mary and her son a lesson for the worlds of their time, so that they would consider them and reflect on their affair, and they would know the greatness of Our power and ability over whatever We will. And it was said one sign and not two signs, and He mentioned two signs because the meaning of the statement is: We made them a sign and an argument for us, so each one of them in the meaning of indicating God and the greatness of His power takes the place of the other, since their affair in indicating God was one.
21:92: God Almighty says: This is your religion, one religion, and I am your Lord, O people, so worship Me, rather than the gods and idols, and whatever else you worship besides Me. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: Your nation is one nation means: Your religion is one religion. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said, regarding his statement: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation, he said: Your religion is one religion, and the second nation was placed in the accusative case for the purpose of separation, and the group of the reciters of the regions read it in the accusative case, and it is correct according to us, because the second nation is indefinite and the first is definite. And since that was the case, and the report before the arrival of the indefinite noun was sufficient, the face of the speech was the accusative, with the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it. It was mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq that he raised that, that he read it as one nation with the intention of repeating the speech, as if he meant: This is your nation, this is one nation.
21:93: God Almighty says: And people were divided in their religion which God commanded them to follow and called them to, so they became parties in it, so the Jews became Jews, the Christians became Christians, and idols were worshipped. Then God Almighty informed us about what they would end up with, and that the return of all the gods of religions is to Him, threatening them with humiliation like the people of deviation and misguidance among them, and teaching them that He is watching them, and that He will reward all of them, the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: And they divided their affair among themselves, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And they divided their affair among themselves, he said: They divided: they differed, in religion.
21:94: God Almighty says: Whoever among those who have divided in their religion does what God has commanded him to do of righteous deeds, and obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions, and he acknowledges the Oneness of God, believes in His promise and His threat, and disavows rivals and gods, there is no denial of his effort. He says: God will thank him for the work he did in obedience to Him, and he believes in Him, so He will reward him in the Hereafter with the reward that He intended for the people of His obedience to reward them, and He will not deny that to him, so he will deny it, and be deprived of his reward for his righteous work. And indeed, We are its recorders. He says: And We write down all of his righteous deeds, and We will not leave anything of them to reward him for their small and large, their little and much. Abu Jaafar said: Ingratitude is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I denied so-and-so his blessings, so I deny him ingratitude and ingratitude. And from this the poet said: There are people who never sleep, and my cheeks are not ungrateful to God.
21:95: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: And it is forbidden. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as and it is forbidden with a kasra on the ha'. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as and it is forbidden with a fatha on the ha' and the alif. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings that agree in meaning, not different. This is because the sacred is the sacred, and the sacred is the sacred, just as the permissible is the permissible, and the permissible is the permissible. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. Ibn Abbas used to read it as and sacred with the interpretation of and resolved. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mu’alla, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who used to recite it and it was forbidden to a village. He said: So I said to Sa’id: What was forbidden? He said: It was determined. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite this verse: “And it has been forbidden to a city which We destroyed that they should not return. So no one of them should return, and no one of them should repent.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they should not return. He said: It is forbidden for any of them to return, that is forbidden for them. Ibn Hamid told us: Isa bin Farqad told us: Jabir al-Ju’fi told us: I asked Abu Ja’far about the return, so he recited this verse: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they should not return. So it is as if Abu Ja’far interpreted that as: And it is forbidden for the people of a town which We have destroyed that they should not return to the world. And the statement which Ikrimah said about that is more correct in my opinion, because God, the Most High, mentioned that people divided their religion with which He sent the Messengers to them, then He informed about His action with those who acted according to what His Messengers called them to of belief in Him and working in obedience to Him, then He followed that with His statement: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they should not return. So if that is report about His action with those who refused to answer His Messengers and worked in disobedience to Him, and the like, it is more likely to be…
21:96: God Almighty says: Until when He opens up the floodgates to Gog and Magog, and they are two nations, He blocks them. As Isam bin Dawud bin Al-Jarrah told me, he said: My father told me, he said: Sufyan bin Saeed Al-Thawri told us, he said: Mansour bin Al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of Rabie bin Jarash, he said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first signs are: the Antichrist, the descent of Jesus, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden Abyan, driving people to the place of assembly, resting with them when they say, and the smoke, and the beast, the price of Gog and Magog.” Hudhayfah said: I said: O Messenger of God, and what are Gog and Magog? He said: Gog and Magog: nations, each nation four hundred thousand, a man of them will not die until he sees a thousand eyes blinking before him from his loins, and they are the children of Adam, so they will march to the destruction of the world, their vanguard will be in Ash-Sham and their rearguard in Iraq, so they will pass by the rivers of the world, and they will drink the Euphrates and the Tigris and the Lake of Tiberias until they reach Jerusalem, and they will say: We have killed the people of the world, so fight those in the heavens, so they will shoot arrows into the heavens, Then their arrows will return stained with blood, and they will say, We have killed those in the heavens, and Jesus and the Muslims have been on Mount Tur for years. Then God, the Most High, will inspire Jesus: Protect My servants on Tur and the area around Ayla. Then Jesus will raise his head to the heavens, and the Muslims will believe, and God will send upon them a beast called Al-Najaf, which will enter through their nostrils, and they will be dead from the edge of Syria to the edge of Iraq, until the earth stinks of their corpses. Then God will command the sky to rain like the mouths of water skins, and it will wash the earth of their corpses and their stench. Then the sun will rise from the west.” Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, who said: Gog and Magog are twice as numerous as all other human beings, and Gog and Magog are two men whose names are Gog and Magog. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Wahb Ibn Jabir narrating, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn `Amr, that he said: The first of Gog and Magog will pass by a river like the Tigris, and the last of them will pass by and say: There was once water in this. Not a single one of them will die except that he will leave behind a thousand or more of his descendants. And he said: After them will be three nations, the number of which is known only to God: Tawil, Taris, and Nasik or Mansik. Shu`bah was not sure. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jabir al-Haywani, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn Amr about Gog and Magog, are they from the children of Adam? He said: Yes, and after them will be three nations whose number is known only to God: Taris, Tawil, and Mansak. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sahl bin Hammad Abu Atab told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Salim: I heard Nafi’ bin Jubayr bin Mut’im say: Abdullah bin Amr said: Gog and Magog have rivers from which they feed whatever they want, women from which they have intercourse with whatever they want, and trees from which they feed whatever they want. No man dies except that he leaves behind a thousand or more descendants. Muhammad bin Amara told us: Abdullah bin Musa told us: Zakariya told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, who said: No one from Gog and Magog died without leaving behind a thousand or more wards. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Atiyya. He said: Abu Saeed said: Gog and Magog will come out and they will not leave anyone without killing him, except the people of the fortresses. They will pass by the lake and drink from it, and the passerby will say: It was as if there was water here. He said: Then God will send upon them the scorpion until it breaks their necks and they will become a mess. The people of the fortresses will say: The enemies of God have perished. They will lead a man to look, and he will stipulate that if he finds them alive, they should lift him up. He will find that they have perished. He said: Then God will send down water from the sky and throw them into the sea, and the earth will be filled with them, and people will plant trees and palm trees after them, and the earth will produce its fruit, as it used to produce in the time of Gog and Magog. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid: Ibn Abbas saw some children jumping on each other while playing, so Ibn Abbas said: This is how Gog and Magog will emerge. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam told us: Amr ibn Qais told us: It has reached us that a king is at the entrance to the dam who sends out cavalry every day to guard the dam, and he does not feel safe from Gog and Magog coming out against them. He said: They hear a commotion and a severe matter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, that Abdullah ibn Amr said: A man of Gog and Magog will not die until a thousand are born to him from his loins. And behind them are three nations whose number is known only to God: Mansak, Tawil, and Taris. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Amr al-Bakali, who said: God divided the angels, mankind, and jinn into ten parts. Nine of them are the Cherubim, who are the angels who carry the Throne. They are also those who glorify God night and day without slackening. He said: And whoever remains of the angels is for the command of God, His revelation, and His message. Then He divided mankind and jinn into ten parts, nine of them are the jinn. No child is born from mankind except that nine are born from the jinn. Then He divided mankind into ten parts, nine of them are Gog and Magog, and the rest of mankind is one part. Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, Until Gog and Magog are let loose, he said: Two nations from behind the dam of Dhul-Qarnayn. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of more than one person, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal, on the authority of Abu al-Sayf, who said: Ka’b said: When Gog and Magog come out, they dig so that those around them can hear the clatter of their axes. Then when night falls, they say: We will come tomorrow and emerge. Then God restores it to how it was. Then they come the next day and find that God has restored it to how it was. Then they dig so that those around them can hear the clatter of their axes. Then when night falls, God casts on the tongue of one of them, saying: We will come tomorrow and emerge, God willing. Then they come the next day and find it to be as they left it. Then they dig and emerge. Then the first group passes by the lake and drinks its water. Then the second group passes by and licks its mud. Then the third group passes by and they say: There was once water here. And the people will flee from them, and nothing will stand up to them. They will throw their arrows to the sky, and they will return covered in blood. They will say: The people of the earth and the people of the sky have defeated us. Then Jesus, son of Mary, will call down curses upon them, saying: O God, we have no power or authority over them, so suffice us against them as you wish. Then God will send upon them a worm called Al-Najaf, which will bite their necks. God will send upon them birds, which will seize them with their beaks and throw them into the sea. God will send a spring called Al-Hayat, which will purify the earth of them and cause it to grow, so much so that even a pomegranate will fill the inhabitants with it. He said: And what is the inhabitants, O Ka’b? He said: The people of the house. He said: While the people were like that, the cry came to them that Dhu al-Sawiqatayn wanted him. So Jesus sent a vanguard of seven hundred, or between seven hundred and eight hundred, until when they were on some of the road, God sent a pleasant Yemeni wind, and God took the soul of every believer in it, then there remained a mass of people who fell as animals fall. So the example of the Hour is like that of a man who circles around his horse waiting for it to give birth. So whoever takes on something after what I have said, or something like this, he is the one who takes on something. Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid Al-Bayrouti told us, he said: My father told me, he said: I heard Ibn Jaber, he said: Muhammad bin Jaber Al-Ta’i told me, then Al-Himsi told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr bin Nafeer Al-Hadrami told me, he said: My father told me that he heard Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Kalabi say: As for his saying, And they will rush forth from every hill, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: What he meant by that is the children of Adam coming out from every place in which they were buried on the earth, and what he meant by that is the gathering to the place where the people will stand on the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They will rush from every hill, he said: The people will be gathered from every place they came from on the Day of Resurrection, so it is the hill. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And they will come down from every side. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: The people will be gathered from every side from the place they came from on the Day of Resurrection, so it is a side. Others said: Rather, he meant Gog and Magog, and his saying and they is a metaphor for their names. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abdul Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, who said: Abu Al-Zura’a told us, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Gog and Magog will emerge and roam the earth, causing corruption in it. Then Abdullah recited: And they will swarm from every mound. He said: Then God will send upon them a beast like a hyena, which will enter their ears and nostrils and they will die from it, and the earth will stink of them. Then God Almighty will send water and purify the earth of them. The correct statement about this is what was said by those who said: He meant Gog and Magog by that, and his saying and they is a metaphor for their names according to the report that: Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar, on the authority of Qatada al-Ansari, then al-Dhafri, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, the brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Gog and Magog will be conquered and will come out upon the people as God said: ‘They will rush forth from every height’ and they will cover the earth.” Ahmad bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham bin Bashir told us: Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muathir, who is Ibn Afazah Al-Abdi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, in what is mentioned about Jesus, son of Mary, he said: “Jesus said: My Lord promised me that the Antichrist will emerge, and that I will descend to him, and he mentioned that he has two sticks with him, and when he sees me, God will destroy him. He said: He will melt as lead melts, until the trees and stones will say: O Muslim, this is an infidel, so kill him. God, the Blessed and Exalted, will destroy them, and the people will return to their lands and homelands, and Gog and Magog will meet them from every hill, swarming, and they will not come upon anything except that they will destroy it, and they will not pass by any water except that they will drink it.” Ubaid bin Ismail Al-Habbari told me: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Asbagh bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Jablah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muathir bin Afazah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. As for his saying, from every slope, he means from every high place, hill, and hill. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, They come from every high place, meaning: They come from every high place. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They come down from every hill. He said: From every hill. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And they come down from every hill, he said: The hill is the elevated thing. And the poet said: Dates on the hump Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm from every mound, he said: This is the beginning of the Day of Resurrection. As for His statement, swarm, it means that they will come out on foot, walking quickly like the swarm of a wolf, as the poet said: The wolf's lions were about to sleep, and the night became cold upon them, so they fled.
21:97: God Almighty says: Until when Gog and Magog are released, the true promise draws near. This is the promise of God who promised His servants that He will raise them from their graves for recompense, reward, and punishment. It is undoubtedly true, as He, the Most High, said. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, meaning Ibn Qais, who told us: Hudhayfah told us: If a man were to commit adultery after the emergence of Gog and Magog, he would not ride it until the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And the true promise has drawn near, he said: The Day of Resurrection has drawn near to them. The waw in His statement, And the true promise has drawn near, is an insertion. The meaning of the statement is: Until when Gog and Magog are released, the true promise has drawn near. This is similar to His statement, So when they had both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead, * And We called to him 37:103-104. Its meaning is: We called to him, changing the waw, as Imru’ al-Qays said: When we passed the courtyard of the neighborhood and we turned towards the valley of Khabt Dhi Haqaf Aqanqal He wants: When we crossed the neighborhood square, he took us aside. And his saying, Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring. There are two aspects to the it in his saying, then behold,: One of them is that it is a metaphor for the eyes, and the apparent eyes are a clarification of them, as the poet said: To Amr, her father, do not let my wife say, Why did Malik bin Abi Kaab flee from me? So he referred to the woman travelling in: For Amr her father, then he made it apparent. The interpretation of the speech then would be: Then the eyes will be fixed, the eyes of those who disbelieved. The second: that it be a pillar, as God Almighty said, For eyes are not blind, and as the poet said: Is it raised by what is here the head? And His statement, Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this, says the Most High: Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed upon the coming of the true promise with its terrors, and the establishment of the Hour with its realities, and they will say, Woe to us! We were before this time in this world heedless of this that we see and witness, and the great affliction that has befallen us. And in the speech there is something omitted that was omitted because the indication of what was mentioned is sufficient for it, and that is what they say regarding His statement, Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed upon us, they will say, Woe to us. And His statement, Rather, we were wrongdoers, is informing us of what those who disbelieved in God on that day said: We did not do for this day what would save us from its hardships, rather we were wrongdoers in our disobedience to our Lord, and our obedience to Satan and his soldiers in the worship of other than God Almighty.
21:98: God Almighty says: You, O polytheists, worship idols and statues besides Him, and whatever gods you worship besides God. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, Indeed, you and what you worship besides God, meaning the gods and those who worship them, are fuel for Hell. As for fuel for Hell, some of them said: Its meaning is: the fuel of Hell and its trees. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, the firewood of Hell means the trees of Hell. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire, meaning: its fuel. Others said: Rather, it means: firewood for Hell. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, fuel of Hell, he said: its firewood. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, and he added to it: And in some readings, firewood of Hell, meaning in the reading of Aisha. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The firewood of Hell. He said: The firewood of Hell that they will be thrown into. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Har, on the authority of Atramah, his statement, The firewood of Hell, he said: The firewood of Hell. Others said: Rather, it means that they will be thrown into Hell. Mention of who said that: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, the pebbles of Hell, that Hell is only stoned with them, and that is the throwing, meaning: they are thrown into it. The readers differed in reading this. The readers of the regions read it as Hasab Jahannam with a sad, and this is the reading according to us, due to the consensus of the authority on it. It was narrated on the authority of Ali and Aisha that they used to recite Dhul-Khatab Jahannam with a ta, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited it Hadhab with a dad. Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to us, he said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he read it like this. It seems that if Ibn Abbas read it like this, he meant that they are the ones who will kindle Hell and ignite it with them, and it is as if everything that the fire is kindled with and ignited with is, according to the Arabs, firewood for it. So if the correct reading is as we mentioned, and the well-known meaning of hasab among the Arabs is throwing, from their saying: hasabt al-rajul if you throw him, as God, the Most High, said: Indeed, We sent upon them a hailstone (al-Qamar 54:34), then the first interpretation of that would be the saying of those who said: Its meaning is that they will be pelted with Hell and thrown into it. It has been mentioned that hasab in the language of the people of Yemen means firewood. If that is like this, then it is also a correct interpretation. As for what we said, that its meaning is throwing, then it is in the language of the people of Najd. As for his saying, You will come to it, its meaning is: You, O people, will come to it or to it. He says: Entering. I have explained the meaning of coming before in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
21:99: God Almighty says to these polytheists, whose description is that they hear no reminder from their Lord except that they listen to it while they are playing, and they are the polytheists of Quraysh 106:You, polytheists, and what you worship besides God are gods that you have not entered, rather they used to prevent whoever wanted to enter them when you were worshipping them in this world. But since they have no benefit for themselves, nor can they ward off harm from themselves, they are further from being humiliated as they are for others. And whoever is like that is clearly far from divinity. And the god is the one who has power over whatever he wills, and nothing has power over him. As for the one who is able to do it, it is not permissible for him to be a god. And His statement, And all therein shall abide eternally means the gods and those who worship them, that they will remain in the Fire forever without end. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: All of you therein shall abide eternally. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, and all therein are eternally therein, he said: The gods that the people worshipped, he said: The worshipper and the worshipped.
21:100: The Almighty means by their saying for them the polytheists and their gods, and the ha and mim in His saying for them are from the mention of all that is in His saying and all therein will abide eternally. The Almighty says: for all of them in Hell is a jug. And therein they will not hear. He says: and they will not hear in the Fire. Ibn Masoud interpreted his statement, And they will not hear therein, as follows: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, he said: Ibn Mas’ud recited this verse: Therein they will have a sigh, and therein they will not hear. He said: When those who will abide in the Fire are thrown into it, they will be put into coffins of fire, then those coffins will be put into other coffins, then the coffins will be put into other coffins in which there are nails of fire, so that none of them will see that there is anyone in the Fire who is being tortured other than him. Then he recited: Therein they will have a sigh, and therein they will not hear. As for his saying, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: He meant by it everyone for whom happiness from God has been granted from among His creation, that he will be removed from the Fire. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Sa`d - not Ibn Mahak - on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hattab, who said: I heard Ali giving a sermon and he recited this verse: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. He said: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, is among them. Others said: Rather, it means: Whoever worships other than God, and he is obedient to God, and is reluctant to worship the one he worships. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Those are far removed from it, he said: Isa, Uzair, and the angels. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Jurayj said: His statement, You and what you worship besides God, then he made an exception and said, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said: He said in Surat al-Anbiya 21:“Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be entering it. If these were gods, they would not have entered it. And all will abide therein eternally. Therein they will have sighing, and therein they will not hear.” Then He made an exception and said: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. The angels were worshipped besides God, and Ezra and Jesus were worshipped besides God. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, Those are far removed from it. He said: Jesus. Ismail bin Saif told me, he said: Ali bin Mashair told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us, he said: Jesus, his mother, Ezra, and the angels. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat, as I have been informed, one day with Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the assembly were more than one man from Quraysh. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke, and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith bit him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to him until he silenced him, then he recited to him and them: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it. If these were gods, they would not have entered it, and all will abide therein eternally”... until His saying: And they will not hear therein. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up, and Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri ibn Qays ibn Adi Al-Sahmi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira said to Abdullah ibn Al-Zubayri: By God, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith did not stand up for Ibn Abdul Muttalib just now, nor did he sit down, and he claimed that I and what we worship of these gods of ours are fuel for Hell. Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayri: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. Ask Muhammad: Will anyone who worships other than God be in Hell with those who worship him? We worship angels, the Jews worship Ezra, and the Christians worship Christ Jesus, son of Mary. Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and those who were in the assembly were amazed at what Abdullah bin Az-Zubayri said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, everyone who loves to be worshipped other than God will be with those who worship Him. They only worship the devils and those who commanded them to worship him. Then God revealed to him: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it... to Immortal: meaning Jesus, son of Mary, Ezra, and those they worshipped from the rabbis and monks who continued in obedience to God, then those who came after them from the people of misguidance took them as lords besides God. Then God revealed, among what they mentioned, that they worship the angels, and that they are the daughters of God, and They said, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants... to His saying: We recompense the wrongdoers. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, who said: Some people say, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, meaning from all people. So it is not like that, rather it means those who worship the gods, and are obedient to God, such as Jesus, his mother, Ezra, and the angels. And God excepted these worshipped gods, who and those who worship them are in the Fire. Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ashqar told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse, Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it, was revealed, the polytheists said: Jesus is being worshipped, and Uzair and the sun are being worshipped. So God revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it, for Jesus and others. The first of the sayings in interpreting this correctly is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by His saying: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it is what was from the deity that the polytheists worshipped, and the deity of God is obedient, and those who worship Him by worshipping Him with God are disbelievers, because the saying of the Most High: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us is the beginning of a statement confirming a matter that some people denied, in the manner that we mentioned in the report, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so it is as if the polytheists said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said to them: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire, the matter is not as you say, because we worship the angels, and others worship the Messiah and Ezra, so the Most High said in response to their saying: Rather, that is so, and those for whom good has preceded from Us are not removed from it, because they are not meant by Our saying: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire. As for the statement of those who said that as an exception to His statement, Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell, this statement has no meaning, because the exception is only to remove the exception from the excepted from, and there is no doubt that those for whom good has preceded from Us are either angels, or humans or jinn, and when the Arabs mention all of these, they mostly mention them with who, not what, and God, the Most High, mentioned only the worshipped ones whom He informed are fuel for Hell with what, He said, Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell, meaning what they used to worship of idols and gods of stones and wood, not of the angels and humans. So if that is the case, then what we have described is that His statement, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us is an answer from God to those who say that what we mentioned of the polytheists is a subject. As for good, it is the active participle of good, and what is meant by it is the happiness that preceded from God for them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us, he said good means happiness, and he said: Happiness preceded for its people from God, and misery preceded for its people from God.
21:101: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it.
21:102: God Almighty says: These people who have received good from Us will not hear the hissing sound of the Fire. What is meant by the hissing sound is the sound and the feeling. If someone were to say: How can they not hear its hissing sound, when you know what was narrated that Hell will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and will let out a sigh, and no one close to God or sent prophet will remain except that he will kneel on his knees in fear of it? It is said: The state in which they hear its hissing sound is not that state, rather it is the state in which: Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, They will not hear its hissing sound, and they will abide eternally in that which their souls desire. He said: The people of Paradise will not hear the hissing sound of the Fire when they descend to their abode in Paradise. And his statement, And they will abide eternally in that which their souls desire. He said: They will abide in that which their souls desire of its pleasures and delights, not fearing leaving it or moving away from it.
21:103: The people of interpretation differed regarding the greater terror: Which terror is it? Some of them said: It is the fire when it envelops its people. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The greatest terror will not grieve them. He said: The Fire when it closes in on its people. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: His statement, The greatest terror will not grieve them, he said: When Hell is closed in, and he said: When death is slaughtered. Others said: Rather, it is the last blast. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, The greatest terror will not grieve them, meaning the final blast. Others said: Rather, that is when the servant is ordered to Hell. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They will not be saddened by the greatest terror. He said: The servant’s turning away to the Fire when he is ordered to do so. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: That will be at the last blast. That is because whoever is not saddened by that greater terror and is safe from it, then it is more likely that he will not be frightened by what comes after it, and whoever is frightened by it is not safe from the terror of what comes after it. And His statement, And the angels will meet them, means: And the angels will meet them, congratulating them, saying, This is your day which you were promised, in which there is honor from God, and favor, and abundant reward for what you used to strive for in this world in obedience to Him. Ibn Zayd said something similar to what we said about that. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, This is your Day which you were promised, he said: This is before they enter Paradise.
