21:104: God Almighty says: The greatest terror will not grieve them, the Day We will roll up the heaven. It will be a Day of Reconciliation for those who grieve them. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the register that God mentioned in this place. Some of them said: It is the name of an angel. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Abu al-Wafa al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding His statement, On the Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for a book, he said: The scroll is an angel, and when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, He says: Write it down as light. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Mu’al told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: I heard Al-Suddi say regarding His statement: On the Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll. He said: The scroll is an angel. Others said: The recorder is a man who used to write for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: Noah bin Qais told us, he said: Amr bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, On the Day when We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for books, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: It is the man. He said: Noah bin Qais told us, he said: Yazid bin Kaab told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The scribe: a writer who used to write for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: Rather, it is the newspaper in which he writes. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, like the folding of a scroll over a book, meaning: like the folding of a page over a book. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day We will fold up the heaven like the folding of a scroll for a book, meaning like the folding of pages. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The register is the document. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On the Day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for a book, he said: The scroll is the page. The first of the sayings on this matter, in our view, that is correct is the saying of the one who said: The register in this place is the newspaper, because that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs, and there is no known scribe for our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose name was the register, nor is there an angel among the angels with that name. If someone says: How do we fold the scroll with the book if the record is a scroll? It is said: The meaning is not like that, but rather its meaning is: On the Day when we fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll on what is in it of the book, then we made folding a source and it was said like the folding of the scroll for the book, the lam in his saying for the book, meaning on. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. Most of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Ja`far the reciter, recited it the day when we fold the sky with a nun. Abu Ja`far recited it the day when the sky is folded with a ta and a damma, in the manner of what the doer was not named. The correct reading in this regard is: what the readers of the regions have said, with the letter nun, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it, and the anomaly of what differs from it. As for the sijil, it is read by all of them with a shaddah on the lam. As for the kitab, the readers of the people of Medina, and some of the people of Kufa and Basra read it with the singular, like folding the sijil for the book. And the majority of the readers of Kufa read it lil-kutub as a collective. The first of the two readings in our view is the correct one: the reading of the one who read it on the basis of the unification of the Book, for what we mentioned of its meaning, for what is meant by it is: like the folding of a scroll on what is written in it, so there is no reason, since that is like its meaning for all books, except for a reason that we follow from the well-known speech of the Arabs. And with His saying like the folding of a scroll, the report of the connection of His saying the greatest terror will not grieve them ends, then the report of what God will do with His creation on that day begins, so He, the Most High, said: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. So the kaf in His saying as is from the connection of We will repeat, which came before it, and the meaning of the speech is: We will repeat the creation naked, barefoot, and uncircumcised on the Day of Resurrection, as We began them the first time, in the state in which We created them in the wombs of their mothers, with the difference of the people of interpretation in the interpretation of that. And what we said about that was said by a group of people of interpretation, and it is the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that is why I chose to say it over others. Mention who said that, and the trace that came in it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The first creation We will repeat he said: barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. Al-Qasim narrated to us: Al-Husayn narrated to us: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The first creation We will repeat, he said: Barefoot, uncircumcised. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibrahim ibn Maysarah informed me that he heard Mujahid say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to one of his wives: They will come to him barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. So she covered herself with her armor and said, Oh, how ugly! Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that Aisha said: O Prophet of God, will people not be modest with one another? He said: Every person on that Day will have something to occupy him. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: People will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Abraham. Then he recited: ‘As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [It is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.’” Ibn Bashar told us: Ishaq bin Yusuf told us: Sufyan told us: Al-Mughira bin Al-Nu’man told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us to give a sermon, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Mughira ibn al-Nu`man al-Nakha`i, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us and mentioned something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Waki` told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, he said: Al-Mughira bin Al-Nu`man Al-Nakha`i told us, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and something similar. Isa bin Yusuf bin Al-Tabbaa Abu Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon and saying: You will meet God on foot, uncircumcised. Abu Kuraib narrated: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me while I was with an old woman from Banu Amir. He said: Who is this old woman, O Aisha? I said: One of my aunts. She said: Ask God to let me enter Paradise. He said: Old people do not enter Paradise. She said: The old woman took what she took and said: God will create them in a creation other than their creation. Then he said: They will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised. She said: God forbid that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, God said: “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. It is a promise binding upon Us”... to the end of the verse. So the first to be clothed will be Abraham, the friend of God. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said: Ubaid God told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir Al-Juhani, he said: The people will be gathered on one plain, their sight will penetrate them and they will hear the caller, barefoot and naked as they were created on the first day. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ibad bin Al-Awam narrated to us, on the authority of Hilal bin Habban, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, “on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, walking, and uncircumcised. I said: O Abu Abdullah, the uncircumcised? He said: The uncircumcised. So one of his wives said: O Messenger of God, will some of us look at the private parts of others? So he said to each one of them on that day what will distract him from looking at the private parts of his brother.” Hilal said: Saeed bin Jubair said: And you have certainly come to Us individually as We created you the first time (al-An’am 6:94). He said: Like the day his mother bore him, everything that was missing from him will be returned to him like the day he was born. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Just as we were and something other than us before we created anything, so we destroy things and return them as perishable, until there is nothing other than us. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, As We began the first creation, We will repeat it... the verse, he said: We will destroy everything as it was the first time. And His statement, A promise binding upon Us, means: We promised you that as a true promise binding upon Us to fulfill what We promised, for We were to do what We promised you of that, O people, because it has already been decreed and decided by Us that We will do it, with certainty that it will happen, so prepare and be ready.
21:105: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the Psalms and the Reminder in this place. Some of them said: What is meant by the Psalms is all the books of the prophets that God sent down to them, and what is meant by the Reminder is the Mother of the Book that is with Him in the heavens. Mention of who said that: Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me, he said: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: I asked Saeed, about the statement of God, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, he said: The remembrance is that which is in the heaven. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, And We have already written in the Psalms, he said: Al-A’mash read it as the Psalms, he said: the Psalms, the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. After the Reminder, he said: the Reminder in heaven. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The Psalms he said: The Book, After the Reminder he said: The Mother of the Book with God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, The Psalms, he said: The Book, After the Reminder, he said: The Mother of the Book with God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We have already written in the Psalms, he said: The Psalms are the books that were revealed to the prophets. And the Reminder is the mother of the book in which things were written before that. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed, regarding his statement, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, he said: We wrote in the Qur’an after the Torah. Others said: Rather, what is meant by the Psalms is the books that God revealed to the prophets after Moses, and by the mention: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance... the verse, he said: The remembrance is the Torah, the Psalms are the books. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, in his statement, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder... the verse, he said: The Reminder is the Torah, and what he meant by the Psalms after the Torah is the Books. Others said: The Psalms are the Psalms of David, and the Torah is the Torah of Moses, peace be upon them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Nathna told us, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that he said regarding this verse: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance. He said: In the Psalms of David, after the remembrance of Moses. The first of these sayings that is most correct in my opinion is what Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said, and those who said the same as them in that, that its meaning is: And We have written in the books after the Mother of the Book in which God wrote everything that is to be, before the creation of the heavens and the earth, and that is as if the Psalms are the book, and it is said from it: I wrote the book and I wrote it, and every book that God sent down to a prophet of His prophets is a reminder. So if that is the case, then in His insertion of the definite article in the reminder, there is clear evidence that it is meant by a specific reminder, known to those addressed by the verse, and if that was not the Mother of the Book that we mentioned, then the Torah would not be more deserving of being meant by that, from the scrolls of Abraham, for it was before the Psalms of David. The interpretation of the statement then, since it was as we described: And We have already decreed, and We have established Our decree in the books after the Mother of the Book, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, means by that: that the land of Paradise will be inherited by those who act in obedience to Him, who abide by His command and prohibition of worship, not those of them who act in disobedience to Him, who prefer obedience to Satan over obedience to Him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hilali told us, he said: Ubaid God bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, he said: The land of Paradise. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. He said: God Almighty informed in the Torah and the Psalms and in His foreknowledge, before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would inherit the earth to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and admit them to Paradise, and they are the righteous. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, he said: We wrote in the Qur’an after the Torah, and the earth is the land of Paradise. Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. He said: The earth is Paradise. Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: I asked Saeed about the statement of God, The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. He said: The land of Paradise. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, that the earth he said: Paradise, My righteous servants will inherit it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, he said: Paradise. And he recited the statement of God, the Most High, “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled for us His promise and made us inherit the earth. We may settle in Paradise wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of the workers.’” (al-Zumar 39:74) He said: So Paradise begins on Earth, then it goes up in degrees, and Hell begins on Earth, and between them is a veil, a wall. No one knows what that wall is. And he recited, A door, its interior contains mercy, and its exterior is before it punishment. (al-Hadid 57:13) He said: And its degrees go down into the Earth, and the degrees of Paradise go up into the heavens. Muhammad bin Awf told us, he said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, he said: Safwan told us, I asked Amer bin Abdullah Abu Al-Yaman: Will the souls of the believers be gathered together? He said: He said: The land about which God says: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, ‘The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.’ He said: It is the land to which the souls of the believers will be gathered until the resurrection. Others said: It is the land that God gives to the believers in this world. Others said: He meant the Children of Israel, because God promised them that and fulfilled it for them. He cited as evidence for his statement the words of God: And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, which We had blessed (al-A’raf 7:137). We have already mentioned the statement of the one who said: The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants, that it is the land of the disbelieving nations, which the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will inherit. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas, from whom Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated.
21:106: God Almighty says: Indeed, in this Qur’an that We revealed to Our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a message for whoever worships God, including the obligations that God has imposed, to His pleasure and the attainment of what is sought from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ward bin Thamamah, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Al-Hadrami, who said: Ka`b told us in this mosque, he said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka`b’s soul, in this there is a message for a people who worship. They are the people or companions of the five prayers. God called them worshippers. Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahan told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Iyas Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ward, on the authority of Ka’b, regarding his statement, Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, he said: Fasting the month of Ramadan, and the five daily prayers. He said: It is filling the hands and the sea with worship. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, he said: Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship: for the nation of Muhammad. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Mu’aya told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, meaning: who work. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship. He said: They say that in this surah is a message. Others say: In the Qur’an there is a revelation of the five obligatory prayers. Whoever performs them has conveyed the message to a people who are worshippers. He said: workers. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed in this is a message for a people who worship, he said: Indeed in this is benefit and knowledge, for a people who worship that message. And His saying, And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, to Our creation except as a mercy to those to whom We have sent you from among My creation. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of this verse. Is it intended to refer to all the world to which Muhammad was sent, including their believers and disbelievers? Or is it intended to refer to the people of faith specifically, without the disbelievers? Some of them said: It refers to all the world, believers and disbelievers. Who said that? Narrated to me by Ishaq bin Shaheen, he said: Narrated to us by Ishaq bin Yusuf al-Azraq, on the authority of al-Mas’udi, on the authority of a man called Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God in His Book, And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, mercy will be written for him in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, will be spared from what befell the nations of subsidence and stoning. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: Mercy was completed for whoever believed in him in this world and the hereafter, and whoever did not believe in him was spared from what afflicted the nations before him. Others said: Rather, it refers to the people of faith, not the people of disbelief. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds, he said: The worlds are those who believed in Him and confirmed Him. He said: And I do not know that it may be a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time, he said, so it is a trial for these people, and a mercy for those people. The command came in general terms as a mercy for the worlds, and the worlds here are those who believed in Him, confirmed Him, and obeyed Him. The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is that God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mercy to the entire world, its believers and its disbelievers. As for the believers, God guided them through him and admitted them into Paradise through faith in him and through acting upon what came from God. As for the disbelievers, He warded off from them the immediate calamity that had befallen the nations that had rejected their messengers before him.
21:107: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
21:108: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: He said, O Muhammad: My Lord has revealed to me nothing but that there is no god for you who may be worshipped except one God, and worship is only appropriate for Him, and it is not appropriate for anyone else. Are you Muslims? He says: Are you submitting to Him, O polytheists, worshippers of idols and statues, by submitting to that, and disavowing the worship of any gods other than Him?
21:109: God Almighty says: If these polytheists, O Muhammad, turn away from the acknowledgment of faith, that they have no god but one God, and turn away from Him and refuse to respond to Him, then say to them, I have given you both notice on equal terms. That is, inform them that you and they know that some of you are at war with others, and that there will be no peace or reconciliation between you. What is meant by this is the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Quraysh, such as: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, But if they turn away, then say, ‘I have warned you on equal terms.’ If they turn away: he means Quraysh. And His statement, And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far, God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, “And I do not know when the time will befall you when God’s punishment which He promised you will come upon you, and He will take revenge on you. Is its coming upon you near or far?” And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far. He said: The appointed time.
21:110: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these polytheists, God knows what you say aloud, and He knows what you conceal, so you do not say aloud. It is the same with Him whether it is hidden or apparent, whether it is secret or public. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. So if He delays His punishment for what you conceal of polytheism with Him, or what you say aloud, then I do not know what the reason is for which He delays it from you? Perhaps He delays it from you, despite His promise to you, as a trial that He wants for you, and so that you may enjoy your life until a term He has set for you which you may reach. Then He will bring down upon you His punishment at that time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And I do not know whether it is a trial for you or an enjoyment for a time. He says: Perhaps what is closer to you than the punishment and the Hour is that it will be delayed for a period of time, and an enjoyment for a time, so my saying that will become a trial for you.
21:111: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time.
21:112: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad: O Lord, judge between me and those of my people who lied about me, disbelieved in You, and worshipped other than You, by bringing Your punishment and vengeance upon them. This is the truth that God Almighty commanded His Prophet to ask his Lord to judge by, and it is similar to His saying, may His praise be glorified: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges. al-A’raf 7:89 And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, He said, ‘My Lord, judge with justice.’ He said: None judges with justice except God, but he only hastened that in this world, asking his Lord about his people. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed a fight, he would say: O Lord, judge with justice. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it as Qal Rabbi Ahkam with a kasra over the ba’ and connected the alif of Ahkam, as a supplication and a question, except for Abu Ja’far, who added a damma over the ba’ of Rabbi, as a singular vocative, and except for Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, as it was narrated from him that he used to recite it as Rabbi Ahkam as a statement that God is more just than every judge, so he would confirm the ya’ in Rabbi Nun and add a hamza to the alif of Ahkam, and raise Ahkam, as a statement of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He. The correct reading in our view is to connect the Baa’ of Ar-Rab and break it with Hakam, and leave the Alif of Ahkam cut off, as is the view of the reciters of the regions, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and the anomaly of what differs from it. As for Ad-Dahhak, in the reading that you mentioned about him there is an extra letter according to the script of the Mushafs, and that should not be added to it, while the meaning of the reading is correct by leaving out its extra letter. Some of them have claimed that the meaning of his saying My Lord, judge with the truth is: Say: My Lord, judge with Your true judgment, then the judgment that the truth is an attribute of was omitted and the truth was established in its place, and for that reason there is a reason, but what we have said is clearer and more similar to what the people of interpretation have said, so that is why we have chosen it. And His saying, And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is the One sought for help against that which you describe, God Almighty says: And say, O Muhammad: And our Lord is He who has mercy on His servants and encompasses them with His favor, Whom I seek help against you in what you say and describe of your saying to me, in what I have brought to you from God, Is this not a human being like you? Do you then practice magic while you see? (Al-Anbiya’: 3), and your saying, Rather, he has invented it; rather, he is a poet (Al-Anbiya’: 5), and in your lying against God Almighty and your saying, The Most Gracious has taken a son (Maryam 19:88 - Al-Anbiya’: 26), then it is easy for Him to change that, and to separate what is between me and you, by hastening the punishment for you, for what you describe of that.
